sources.title: Dabur India Limited vs Patanjali Ayurved Limited And Anr on 3 July, 2025 (CS(COMM) 1195/2024)
sources.note: Judgment of Mini Pushkarna J. on interim applications in Dabur's suit alleging that Patanjali's television and print advertisements for "Patanjali Special Chyawanprash" disparaged "Dabur Chyawanprash" and Chyawanprash generally by calling rival products "ordinary". Finds a strong prima facie case of disparagement and directs Patanjali to delete the specified disparaging lines from the TVC and print advertisements; other issues (use of "special", "51 precious herbs", mercury claims) left to trial.

sources.title: Delhi High Court restrains Patanjali from airing advertisements disparaging Dabur Chyawanprash
sources.note: Reports the 3 July 2025 interim order.

sources.title: Patanjali Moves Delhi HC Against Order Restraining It From Airing Ads Disparaging Dabur Chyawanprash
sources.note: Reports Patanjali's intra-court appeal against the 3 July 2025 single-judge order; appeal status not further confirmed.

sources.title: Patanjali restrained from calling other chyawanprash brands as 'dhoka'; Delhi High Court grants interim relief to Dabur
sources.note: Reports a further interim order restraining a Star Plus advertisement in which Patanjali called other Chyawanprash "dhoka" (deception).

sources.title: Ramdev's Patanjali Removes Sharbat Jihad Ad After Delhi HC Warning
sources.note: Reports the 22 April 2025 hearing before Amit Bansal J. in Hamdard National Foundation India v. Patanjali Foods Limited, CS(COMM) 356/2025, over a video in which Ramdev used the phrase "sharbat jihad" against Hamdard's Rooh Afza while promoting Patanjali's Gulab Sharbat; the video was taken down.

sources.title: 'Sharbat Jihad': Delhi HC Mulls Contempt Notice For Baba Ramdev
sources.note: Records the court's remark that the video "shocks the conscience of the court" and its warning that it would consider contempt if disparaging videos continued.

sources.title: Delhi HC Disposes Suit Against Baba Ramdev Over "Sharbat Jihad" Remark
sources.note: Reports Amit Bansal J.'s disposal of CS(COMM) 356/2025 on 9 May 2025 after Patanjali affirmed on affidavit that the video had been permanently taken down.

sources.title: Madras HC Restrains Patanjali From Using 'Coronil' Trademark [Read Order]
sources.note: Reports the ex-parte interim injunction of 17 July 2020 by C.V. Karthikeyan J. in O.A. No. 258 of 2020 (Arudra Engineers Pvt Ltd v Patanjali Ayurved Ltd), restraining use of "Coronil" on the ground that the mark 'CORONIL-92 B' was registered by the plaintiff since 1993.

sources.title: Patanjali exploited public fear says Madras HC, imposes Rs 10 lakh fine
sources.note: Reports the 6 August 2020 order making the interim injunction in O.A. No. 258 of 2020 absolute and imposing a Rs 10 lakh cost, the judge remarking that Patanjali was "exploiting the fear and panic among the general public" by projecting Coronil as a cure rather than an immunity booster; cost ordered split between the Adyar Cancer Institute and a government naturopathy hospital.

sources.title: [CORONIL case] Registration of trademark does not confer monopoly over part of it: Madras High Court lifts injunction on Patanjali Ayurved
sources.note: Reports the Division Bench's order in O.S.A. No. 169 of 2020 setting aside the single judge's injunction, holding that no prima facie case of trademark infringement was made out against Patanjali and that registration of a composite mark does not confer a monopoly over each component.

sources.title: Madras High Court Sets Aside Injunction Order Against Patanjali Ayurved
sources.note: Law-firm case note giving the citation Patanjali Ayurveda Ltd. & Anr. v. Arudra Engineers Pvt. Ltd., O.S.A. No. 169 of 2020, decision dated 2 February 2021.

sources.title: Govt allows Ramdev to market Patanjali's Coronil as immunity booster, not authorised for Covid-19 therapy
sources.note: Reports the Ministry of AYUSH's position that Coronil is licensed only as an immunity booster and not authorised as a Covid-19 treatment; used only as background for the events list, not as an adverse claim.

sources.title: Hamdard National Foundation India v. Patanjali Foods Limited and Anr., CS(COMM) 356/2025 (order of 22 April 2025)
sources.note: Official order of Amit Bansal J. Records, at para 17, defendants' counsel submitting on instructions that "the impugned advertisements in the video format shall be immediately taken down" and that print advertisements would be altered or removed, with a compliance affidavit due in five days; at para 18, directs both defendants to file affidavits that they will not issue similar disparaging statements, social media posts or videos against competitors' products in future.

sources.title: Arudra Engineers Private Limited v. Patanjali Ayurved Limited, O.A. No. 258 of 2020 in C.S. No. 163 of 2020 (order of 6 August 2020)
sources.note: Judgment of C.V. Karthikeyan J. dismissing Patanjali's applications (A. Nos. 1532 and 1533 of 2020) to suspend and vacate the 17 July 2020 ex-parte interim injunction; restrains Patanjali from using the mark "Coronil" or any deceptive variation pending disposal of the suit and orders costs paid jointly to specified charitable institutions.

sources.title: Indian Medical Association vs Union Of India on 27 August, 2024 (W.P.(C) No. 645/2022)
sources.publisher: Supreme Court of India (Indian Kanoon copy)
sources.note: Record of proceedings before Hima Kohli and Sandeep Mehta JJ recording that only 10 States/UTs, including Uttarakhand, had complied with the Court's order of 30 July 2024 on advertising self-certification and the Ministry of AYUSH's complaint dashboard; confirms the existence and substance of the 30 July 2024 order.

sources.title: A self-styled faith healer held for raping Punjab woman
sources.note: Contemporaneous report of the arrest at Delhi airport. Names Zirakpur SHO inspector Pawan Kumar; records the April 2018 complaint, the look-out notice, production before a Mohali court and two-day police remand, and lists the FIR sections as IPC 376, 420, 354, 294, 323 and 506 with section 67 of the IT Act. Names six aides in the FIR (Jatinder, Akbar, Sartar Ali, Sucha Singh, Rajesh Chaudhary, Sandeep Pehlwan).

sources.title: Warrant against pastor Bajinder in 2018 case
sources.note: Non-bailable warrant issued on 3 March 2025 by Additional District and Sessions Judge Harsimranjit Singh at Mohali; next hearing 18 March 2025. Gives the FIR date at Zirakpur police station as 20 April 2018 and names the co-accused.

sources.title: Pastor Bajinder Singh held guilty in 2018 rape case, verdict on April 1
sources.note: Conviction on 28 March 2025 by Additional District and Sessions Judge Vikrant Kumar under IPC 376, 323 and 506; five co-accused acquitted (Jatinder Kumar, Akbar Bhatti, Rajesh Chaudhary, Sitar Ali, Sandeep Pehlwan). Also records the 3 March 2025 non-bailable warrants, the Kapurthala FIR of 28 February 2025 and the Majri FIR of 25 March 2025 with its BNS sections.

sources.title: Pastor Bajinder Singh awarded life imprisonment in 2018 rape case
sources.note: Sentence of 1 April 2025: life imprisonment under IPC 376 and one year each under IPC 323 and 506, to run concurrently. Quotes the sentencing order at length ("Sexual violence, apart from being a dehumanising act, is an unlawful intrusion on the right of privacy and sanctity of a female...") and records counsel H S Dhanoa's statement that the verdict would be challenged in the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

sources.title: Heinous offence: Pastor Bajinder given life imprisonment for rape
sources.note: Describes the sentence as life imprisonment till death with a fine of Rs 1 lakh; names the five acquitted co-accused; records the plea for leniency and the statements of the survivor and of counsel for both sides.

sources.title: 'Yeshu Yeshu' fame pastor Bajinder Singh gets life term in 2018 rape case
sources.note: Same-day report of the sentence; notes that the Kapurthala case was then still to reach court.

sources.title: 'Yeshu Yeshu' Fame Self-Styled Pastor Bajinder Singh Gets Life Imprisonment In 2018 Rape Case
sources.note: Legal-news report of the conviction and sentence. It states "A detailed order is awaited" and does not attach a copy of the judgment, so it does not serve as a court source.

sources.title: Punjab: Preacher Bajinder Singh sentenced to life in 2018 rape case
sources.note: Independent summary of the conviction and sentence; describes the two churches at Tajpur and Majri.

sources.title: Pastor Bajinder Singh booked for sexual harassment, Christian community says conspiracy, stages protest
sources.note: Sets out the Kapurthala complaint in detail and the sections applied (IPC 354-A, 354-D, 506), confirmed by SHO Bikramjit Singh; carries Christian leader Avtar Singh's statement that the FIR is false and part of a conspiracy.

sources.title: SIT to probe sexual harassment charges against pastor Bajinder Singh
sources.note: Three-member SIT constituted on 3 March 2025 under Phagwara SP Roopinder Kaur with DSP (SD) Deep Karan Singh and Kapurthala (City) SHO Bikramjit Singh; SSP Gaurav Toora quoted. Carries Bajinder Singh's denial in his own words. This report also states, incorrectly and before the trial ended, that he had been acquitted in the 2018 case.

sources.title: Women panel seeks report in pastor case
sources.note: Punjab State Women's Commission chairperson Raj Lalli Gill took suo motu notice and asked the Kapurthala SSP for a status report by 6 March 2025 and for the complainant's security.

sources.title: National Commission for Women calls for arrest of pastor Bajinder
sources.note: Quotes the NCW's post on X of 7 March 2025 recording suo motu cognisance under chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar, the demand for arrest and victim protection, and for the action-taken report and FIR copy within three days. Also records that the Kapurthala FIR was registered on 28 February 2025.

sources.title: Pastor Bajinder Singh case: Victim appears before NCW
sources.note: The Kapurthala complainant appeared before the National Commission for Women on 25 March 2025.

sources.title: Punjab: Now, 'Pastor' Bajinder booked for assault after woman in 'viral video' files complaint
sources.note: FIR of 25 March 2025 at Majri police station, Mullanpur, under BNS 74, 115(2) and 351(2), confirmed by SHO inspector Sunil Kumar; complainant a 40-year-old who had served in the ministry for 13-14 years and says the incident occurred on 14 February 2025.

sources.title: Already in Mansa jail for rape, pastor now faces probe in Bharatpur conversion case
sources.note: Bharatpur FIR at Atal Bandh police station under IPC 295A, 298, 323 and 120-B, with 153A added later, over an assembly of 11 February 2024 at Sonar Haveli. Records the production warrant, the appearance before the Bharatpur court on 23 August 2025, 15 days' judicial custody at Sewar jail and return to Mansa jail, quoting Mansa Jail Deputy Superintendent Jagjit Singh and complainant's counsel Uttam Sharma. Summarises a police progress report seen by the paper. Also lists a 2021 NCPCR inquiry.

sources.title: Rs 2 crore seized in raids on pastors Bajinder Singh, Harpreet Deol in Punjab
sources.note: Income Tax searches of 1 February 2023 at six or seven premises in Jalandhar, Amritsar and New Chandigarh, running 6 am to 10 pm; officials quoted on unaccounted cash of about Rs 2 crore and on lines of inquiry into donations, offshore centres and foreign funding.

sources.title: Amid hustle-bustle, BJP quietly reaches out to 'miracle performing' pastors
sources.note: Records that BJP Gurdaspur candidate Dinesh Singh Babbu attended a Bajinder Singh congregation in Chandigarh during the 2024 Lok Sabha campaign, that BJP Minority Morcha state president Thomas Masih sought votes for Babbu from Bajinder Singh's stage, that BJP Amritsar candidate Taranjit Singh Sandhu attended a Bajinder Singh congregation at Ajnala on 30 April 2024, and that BJP Ajnala leader and former MLA Amarpal Singh Boni spoke at Bajinder Singh's "Amritsar Crusade". Also dates the Income Tax raid to 1 February 2023.

sources.title: Who is Papa Bajinder Singh? Punjab's pastor behind viral Yeshu Yeshu videos, named in sex harassment case
sources.note: Profile: conversion in prison during a murder case, release in 2012, Tajpur church founded 2014 with 23 branches in Punjab and branches in Canada, the UK and Dubai; the 2018 arrest at Indira Gandhi International Airport en route to London and subsequent bail.

sources.title: Controversies, cases, viral clips: All about self-styled Punjab pastor Bajinder Singh
sources.note: Only located report of pre-2018 cases: a 2014 booking under IPC 295A at Karnal and charges of assault and intimidation dating to 2006 in Yamunanagar, Haryana, and imprisonment in a murder case from 2008. Gives the Kapurthala complaint date as 20 February and the FIR date as 23 February 2025, which differs from The Indian Express and The Tribune (28 February 2025).

sources.title: Victim in pastor Bajinder Singh rape case says she was forced to relocate frequently, faced 3 cases while suing him
sources.note: On-record interview with the complainant in the 2018 case about the seven-year proceedings, and background on the ministry's finances and 260 claimed branches.

sources.title: Pastor's aides put off protest to March 26
sources.note: Christian organisations with Valmiki and Mazhabi Sikh groups postponed a "Punjab bandh" call, termed the Kapurthala case "false" and demanded a fair probe by the SIT.

sources.title: Parties find it hard to ignore growing influence of self-styled pastors of Pentecostal churches
sources.note: Year-end review placing the March 2025 conviction in the context of Punjab party outreach to Pentecostal churches before the 2027 Assembly election. Also refers in passing to Enforcement Directorate raids on his properties in a money-laundering matter; no ED press release or other corroboration for that was located, so it is not recorded as a claim in this file.

sources.title: Self-styled Punjab pastor Bajinder Singh lands into another controversy as his video assaulting woman goes viral
sources.note: Describes the circulated clip in which he is seen striking a man and slapping a woman holding a toddler. The paper states it has not independently verified the authenticity of the video.

sources.title: KUMAR v. BOCHASANWASI SHRI AKSHAR PURUSHOTTAM SWAMINARAYAN SANSTHA, INC., 3:21-cv-11048 (D.N.J.) — docket
sources.publisher: United States District Court for the District of New Jersey via CourtListener/RECAP
sources.note: Full docket. Filed 11 May 2021; District Judge Georgette Castner (originally Anne E. Thompson), Magistrate Judge Tonianne J. Bongiovanni; cause 29:201 Fair Labor Standards Act; nature of suit 710. Records the 23 November 2021 stay, the 10 December 2021 administrative termination, the second amended complaint of 3 February 2022, the October 2023 voluntary dismissal by twelve plaintiffs, the 28 October 2025 order reopening the case and lifting the stay, and the motions to dismiss at ECF 115, 152 and 154. Docket last updated 4 September 2026.

sources.title: Collective and Class Action Complaint, Kumar v. BAPS, No. 3:21-cv-11048 (D.N.J.), ECF 1
sources.publisher: United States District Court for the District of New Jersey via CourtListener/RECAP
sources.note: 42-page complaint by Mukesh Kumar, Keshav Kumar, Devi Laal, Niranjan, Pappu and Brajendra. Six causes of action: TVPA (18 U.S.C. 1595, pleading violations of 18 U.S.C. 1589, 1590, 1592(a), 1594(a), 1594(b) and 1597(a)); FLSA minimum wage and overtime; N.J.S.A. 34:11-56a et seq.; N.J.S.A. 34:11-4.4 et seq.; unjust enrichment; quantum meruit. Alleges more than 200 R-1 workers, 87-hour weeks, about $450 a month or roughly $1.20 an hour, passports confiscated on arrival, a fenced and guarded compound, and recruitment from Scheduled Caste and other marginalised communities. Names the death of one R-1 worker, Moham Lal.

sources.title: Letter from Andrew I. Glenn to Magistrate Judge Bongiovanni, Kumar v. BAPS, ECF 79
sources.publisher: United States District Court for the District of New Jersey via CourtListener/RECAP
sources.note: Plaintiffs' counsel reports that the government "investigation is still open" with no timeframe for conclusion, and that the case "has been stalled for over four years"; announces the motion to lift the TVPA stay under 18 U.S.C. 1595(b) or to sever the wage-and-hour claims.

sources.title: Letter from Paul J. Fishman for the BAPS defendants, Kumar v. BAPS, ECF 81
sources.publisher: United States District Court for the District of New Jersey via CourtListener/RECAP
sources.note: Counsel for the BAPS defendants informs the court that in conversations on 15 and 16 September 2025 attorneys for the government "advised that DOJ has closed its investigation of BAPS and the other entities and individuals named as defendants in this lawsuit", so there is "no longer a basis on which to continue the stay". The same letter records that on 11 May 2021 the Department of Justice and various federal investigative agencies conducted a search at the Robbinsville mandir.

sources.title: Lawsuit claims New Jersey Hindu temple was built on forced labor
sources.note: Doreen Holder, a spokesperson for the FBI's Newark field office, confirmed the agents' presence at the temple, saying only that the FBI was on scene "on court-authorized law enforcement activity". Carries BAPS spokesperson Matthew Frankel's statement and, at second hand from The New York Times, the statements of BAPS spokesperson Lenin Joshi and chief executive Kanu Patel.

sources.title: Hindu temple in New Jersey accused of "shocking" violations of forced labor laws in lawsuit
sources.note: Reports the FBI's "court-authorized law enforcement activity" statement and that Homeland Security Investigations declined to comment.

sources.title: Suit: Workers lured to N.J. from India paid $1.20 per hour for years
sources.publisher: Associated Press (David Porter and Mallika Sen) via WHYY
sources.note: An FBI spokesperson confirmed agents were at the temple on "court-authorized law enforcement activity" but would not elaborate; one of the attorneys who filed the suit said some workers were removed from the site on 11 May 2021. Carries Matthew Frankel's statement for BAPS.

sources.title: Human trafficking suit spreads to Hindu temples in five US states
sources.note: Reports the amended complaint extending the claims to BAPS sites in other states and quotes a lawyer for the organisation that "US Government officials have authorised the use of R-1 visas for stone artisans for 20 years, and federal, state, and local government agencies have regularly visited and inspected all of the construction projects on which those artisans volunteered".

sources.title: 'Workers Exploited By BAPS': Calls For Justice as US Govt Concludes Probe
sources.note: Reports the court filing in which BAPS's lawyer said government attorneys had informed him that the "DOJ has closed its investigation of BAPS and the other entities and individuals named as defendants in this lawsuit", and records that the Dalit Solidarity Forum and other groups under the Savera umbrella called for a full investigation into BAPS's recruitment and contracting practices.

sources.title: Yoga guru Bikram Choudhury must pay $900,000 to former employee, jury decides
sources.note: Stephen Ceasar. Reports the 25 January 2016 jury verdict awarding Minakshi Jafa-Bodden about $924,500 in compensatory damages, the jury's finding of malice, oppression and fraud, and Choudhury's sworn denial of the sexual-assault allegations. Notes the LA County DA's 2013 decision not to prosecute for lack of corroborating evidence.

sources.title: Yoga guru Bikram Choudhury must pay $6.4 million in punitive damages, jury decides
sources.note: Stephen Ceasar. Reports the 26 January 2016 punitive-damages verdict of more than $6.4 million against Choudhury, on top of the $924,500 compensatory award; records that six other women had filed civil suits alleging sexual assault, that one had reached a conditional settlement, and that five remained pending.

sources.title: He Faced Allegations of Sexual Assault and Rape From Students for Years. Now Bikram Choudhury is ...
sources.note: Renee Marie Schettler. States the Jafa-Bodden award totalled more than $7.4 million; that about sixteen months later Choudhury's failure to pay resulted in a warrant for his arrest; that he filed for bankruptcy; and that he has continued to lead yoga teacher trainings in India, Thailand and Mexico. Also records that at least three of the other lawsuits were settled out of court and that the rest were left pending after he left the country.

sources.title: In re: Bikram's Yoga College of India LP, a limited partnership, No. 9:17-bk-12045
sources.publisher: United States Bankruptcy Court, Central District of California (PACER via CourtListener/RECAP)
sources.note: Chapter 11 petition filed 9 November 2017 by Bikram's Yoga College of India LP; case terminated 26 June 2023. The docket lists Minakshi Jafa-Bodden as a secured/judgment creditor (including a Chapter 11 trustee's motion to approve a compromise with "Secured Creditor Minakshi Jafa-Bodden") and records an objection by "Judgment Creditor Petra Starke Smeltzer" to that compromise.

sources.title: Chandraswami And K.N. Aggarwal vs Central Bureau Of Investigation ... on 23 December, 1999
sources.note: Anil Dev Singh J. Disposes of Crl. Rev. 283/97 (Chandraswami and K.N. Aggarwal against framing of charges), Crl. Rev. 385/97 (CBI against discharge of K.K. Tewari and P.V. Narasimha Rao) and Crl. Rev. 341/97 (PUCL, same). Records that the CBI case was that between 1988 and October 1989 Chandraswami, Aggarwal, Rao, Tewari and others conspired to forge evidence of an account opened by Ajeya Singh (V.P. Singh's son) at First Trust Corporation Ltd, St Kitts; the trial court framed charges against Chandraswami and Aggarwal under IPC 120-B/195/469/471 on 4 June 1997 while discharging Tewari and Rao for insufficient evidence. The High Court holds "I am not persuaded to hold that Shri Chandraswami was not rightly chargesheeted by the trial court" and upholds the discharge of Rao and Tewari.

sources.title: Enforcement Directorate vs Nemi Chand Jain @ Chandraswami [Along with connected matters] on 31 January, 2008
sources.note: Sanjay Kishan Kaul J. Records that in FERA/FCRA adjudication proceedings a penalty of "Rs. 9.65 crores" was imposed on Chandraswami, unpaid, with an SLP against it pending; that ten separate criminal complaints for FERA/FCRA violations under s.8(1) read with s.56 FERA were pending against him; and that "the respondent, in fact, stands acquitted in the Lakhu Bhai Pathak's case and there is nothing else pending in that behalf." Grants conditional permission to travel abroad in the pending FERA/FCRA cases.

sources.title: Chronology of Lakhubhai Pathak case
sources.note: Detailed dated chronology: FIR 5 Feb 1988; chargesheet against Chandraswami and Aggarwal 12 April 1996; CMM frames charges 21 May 1996; Rao made an accused, charges framed against all three 6 November 1996; and "December 22: Special Judge Dinesh Dayal acquits Rao, Chandraswami and Mamaji." Accessed via its Google News syndication link; original at rediff.com.

sources.title: The pickle that proved too spicy
sources.note: Background on the Lakhubhai Pathak allegation (USD 100,000 paid to Chandraswami on 4 January 1984 on the promise of a government paper-pulp contract) with an added note that "Special Judge D Dayal announced his verdict in a courtroom set up at the high-security Vigyan Bhavan annexe in New Delhi on Monday. Rao, Chandraswami and Mamaji were acquitted." Accessed via its Google News syndication link; original at rediff.com.

sources.title: ₹70cr St Kitts scam that nearly ruined an honest PM: VP Singh and his son took hit; real culprits walked free
sources.note: Anjali Rajgovind. Full narrative of the St Kitts affair, with: 26 September 1996 CBI chargesheet naming Rao, Chandraswami, Mamaji and K.K. Tewari; June 1997 discharge of Rao and Tewari and formal framing of charges against Chandraswami and Mamaji; trial opened 28 July 1997; prosecution closed evidence 4 April 2004; Mamaji died 31 August 2004; "On 25 October 2004, Special Judge Dinesh Dayal delivered his verdict: Chandraswami acquitted," the court finding the documents were forged but that the prosecution could not prove who forged them. Accessed via its Google News syndication link; original at bhaskarenglish.in.

sources.title: Controversial godman Chandraswami is no more
sources.note: Obituary. States he "was arrested in 1996 for allegedly defrauding a businessman in London" and "also faced multiple charges of Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) from the Enforcement Directorate (ED)"; that the Supreme Court lifted a travel ban in 2009; and that "In June 2011, the ED had imposed a fine of Rs 9 crore on Chandraswami for FERA violations." Accessed via its Google News syndication link; original at deccanherald.com.

sources.title: Delhi Court Orders Framing of Charges against Daati Maharaj and His Two Brothers in Rape Case
sources.note: Detailed timeline: complaint filed 7 June 2018, FIR registered 11 June 2018; Delhi Police chargesheet named Daati Maharaj, Ashok, Arjun and Anil, October 2018; Delhi HC transferred probe to CBI 3 October 2018; CBI supplementary chargesheet added Neetu alias Maa Shraddha and Neema Joshi; bail granted to Daati Maharaj and three brothers 22 January 2019 (Rs 1 lakh bond each, conditions on contact/travel); Saket Court (Judge Neha) frames charges against Daati Maharaj, Ashok and Arjun on 20 September 2024, discharges Anil; accused deny charges and claim trial; prosecution evidence recording to begin 18 October 2024.

sources.title: Court frames charges against Daati Maharaj, two others in 2018 rape case
sources.note: ANI wire report corroborating the September 2024 charge-framing; the complaint alleged the victim was raped in 2016 and repeatedly raped at "Gurukul Ashwasan" in Bal Gram, Rajasthan; case registered under IPC 376, 377, 506 "etc." against Daati Maharaj and others; she said she had not complained earlier out of intimidation.

sources.title: CBI Moves Delhi HC Against Bail Granted To Daati Maharaj In Rape Case
sources.note: Justice Chander Shekhar of the Delhi High Court directed Daati Maharaj to file a reply within four weeks to the CBI's challenge (CRL.M.C. 989-992/2019) to the anticipatory bail, the CBI arguing the Additional Sessions Judge "erroneously granted anticipatory bail while reviewing a disposed off matter"; notes the HC had earlier rejected his plea to keep the case with Delhi Police, saying the investigation "casts a shadow" on it; next listed for 11 December 2019.

sources.title: Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Daati Madanlal & Daati Maharaj on 26 February, 2019
sources.note: Justice Chander Shekhar. CBI's petitions CRL.M.C. 989-992/2019 (with CRL.M.As. 3935-3949 of 2019) against Daati Madanlal alias Daati Maharaj, Ashok, Arjun and Anil respectively; adjourned for amendment application, renotify 20 March 2019.

sources.title: Central Bureau Of Investigation vs Daati Madanlal & Daati Maharaj on 21 February, 2019
sources.note: Justice Chander Shekhar. Same CRL.M.C. 989-992/2019 petitions listed and renotified for 26 February 2019.

sources.title: CBI files status report in case against Daati Maharaj
sources.note: CBI filed a status report in the sexual-assault case before the Delhi High Court.

sources.title: I have been framed by 3 ex-aides, Daati Maharaj
sources.note: Report on Daati Maharaj's denial during police questioning, in which he said three former aides had framed him.

sources.title: Witness in rape case against Daati Maharaj alleges threats
sources.note: Prime witness Sachin Jain lodged a police complaint alleging he was intercepted by men in an SUV and threatened not to give evidence or speak to media against Daati Maharaj.

sources.title: Sexual assault case, SC asks Daati Maharaj to move HC with his grievances
sources.note: Supreme Court declined to entertain Daati Maharaj's challenge and directed him to approach the Delhi High Court.

sources.title: Nagpur police give 'clean chit' to Bageshwar Dham chief in complaint lodged by anti-superstition crusader
sources.note: Names the complainant (Shyam Manav, founder of Akhil Bharatiya Andhashraddha Nirmoolan Samiti), the complaint date (8 January 2023), the laws invoked (Maharashtra Black Magic Act 2013 and Drugs and Magic Remedies Act 1954), and quotes Nagpur Police Commissioner Amitesh Kumar that the programme did not attract action under either law; also carries Shastri's "anyone can challenge" response to ANI.

sources.title: Nagpur police give clean chit to Bageshwar Dham chief Dhirendra Shastri in complaint lodged by anti-superstition crusader
sources.note: Corroborates the Nagpur police finding of no offence.

sources.title: Deepak Dilip Jagdev vs Home Minister of State Maharashtra and Ors, WP No. 5497 of 2023
sources.publisher: Bombay High Court via Indian Kanoon
sources.note: Bench of R.D. Dhanuka and Gauri Godse JJ. Petitioner sought action against the Maharashtra Home Minister for not acting against Shastri over programmes at Nagpur (7-8 Jan 2023) and Mira Road (18-19 March 2023); records that Mira Road police had already been granted permission for the programme on 16 March 2023, that no complaint of any nature had been made about the Nagpur programme and no untoward incident occurred there, and that the Senior PI would attend and videograph the Mira Road event. The court dismissed the petition as not bonafide and "politically motivated", without impleading Shastri as a party, while directing police to act if any offence were in fact found.

sources.title: Bageshwar Dham: पंडित धीरेंद्र शास्त्री बोले- कुंभलगढ़ दुर्ग पर लगा हरा झंडा उतारकर भगवा फहराओ, उदयपुर में FIR
sources.note: FIR registered at Hathipol police station, Udaipur, under IPC 153A after Shastri said at a Gandhi Ground meeting on 23 March 2023 that the green flags atop Kumbhalgarh Fort should be replaced with saffron ones; a second FIR was registered at Kelwada police station, Rajsamand district, over the same remarks.

sources.title: बागेश्वर धाम के धीरेंद्र शास्त्री के बयान के बाद कुंभलगढ़ दुर्ग पर फहराया जा रहा था भगवा झंडा, 5 गिरफ्तार
sources.note: Five youths arrested for trying to hoist a saffron flag at Kumbhalgarh Fort after Shastri's remarks; additional SP Chandrasheel Thakur is quoted.

sources.title: Complaint lodged against Bageshwar Dham Sarkar with Mumbai police for controversial statement about Shirdi Sai Baba
sources.note: Yuva Sena (UBT) leader Rahul Narain Kanal's written complaint at Bandra police station, 3 April 2023, over Shastri's remark that Sai Baba could be called a saint or fakir but not God; sought action including under IPC 153A.

sources.title: Complaint lodged against Bageshwar Dham Sarkar with Mumbai police for controversial statement about Shirdi Sai Baba
sources.note: Corroborates the Bandra police station complaint over the Sai Baba remark; reports an FIR was registered.

sources.title: Bihar BJP leader moves court over 'derogatory' language against godman
sources.note: Reports the Muzaffarpur ACJM court petitions arising from Shastri's planned Patna visit; distinguishes the petition against Shastri from a separate petition filed on his behalf.

sources.title: PM Modi lays foundation stone of cancer hospital at Bageshwar Dham
sources.note: Corroborates the foundation-stone ceremony and hospital details.

sources.title: बागेश्वर धाम सरकार की सुरक्षा में बढ़ोतरी, धीरेंद्र कृष्ण शास्त्री को मिली Y केटेगरी की सिक्योरिटी

sources.title: Video of Dhirendra Shastri arriving in Raipur in govt aircraft, cop touching his feet sparks row
sources.note: Shastri, accompanied by Chhattisgarh State Minister Guru Khushwant Saheb, arrived in Raipur in a state government aircraft for a religious discourse in Bhilai; a police officer in uniform saluted the minister then touched Shastri's feet. Congress called it "misuse of public money"; the BJP called the officer's gesture personal faith.

Pinto) declined an urgent hearing of a PIL seeking directions to police to prevent hate speech during Shastri's 26 May-7 June 2023 programmes in Surat, Ahmedabad, Vadodara and Rajkot; records the petitioner's claim that he had by then also been booked in Udaipur and that similar demands followed his programmes in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Bihar.

sources.title: Daiichi Sankyo Company Ltd v. Malvinder Mohan Singh and others, SLP(C) 20417/2017, Contempt Petition (C) 2120/2018 and Suo Motu Contempt Petition (C) 4/2019
sources.publisher: Supreme Court of India via Indian Kanoon
sources.note: Reportable judgment of Chief Justice Uday Umesh Lalit with Indira Banerjee and K.M. Joseph JJ. Records at paragraph 18 the oral submissions of senior counsel Arvind Datar for Daiichi that "Mr. Gurinder Singh Dhillon and Mr. Gurpreet Singh Dhillon are unitholders of RHT", that Gurpreet Singh Dhillon was an executive director and chief executive officer of RHT, that they are close relatives of the Singh brothers and that "it is probable that the Dhillon family … also benefitted from the FHL-IHH-RHT transaction". Also records that Contemnor No. 9, Malvinder Mohan Singh, seeking to purge his contempt, submitted a table of loans extended by Modland Wears, Devera Developers, Fern Healthcare, Best Healthcare and Adept Lifespaces to members of the Dhillon family and to Sunil and Sanjay Godhwani, totalling Rs 998.3 crore, of which Rs 1.57 crore is shown against Gurinder Singh Dhillon, as properties that could still be proceeded against. The list of dates records that the Master Purchase Agreement of 12 February 2018 for the acquisition of RHT assets for Rs 4,650 crore "was endorsed by Gurpreet Singh Dhillon on behalf of RHT". These are recorded submissions of parties, not findings against any member of the Dhillon family; the Court sentenced Malvinder and Shivinder Mohan Singh and made no order against any Dhillon.

sources.title: Daiichi Sankyo Company Ltd v. Malvinder Mohan Singh and others, O.M.P.(EFA)(COMM.) 6/2016, Neutral Citation 2023:DHC:2688
sources.publisher: High Court of Delhi via Indian Kanoon
sources.note: Judgment of Justice Yashwant Varma dismissing objections by Fortis Hospitals Ltd and Indiabulls Housing Finance Ltd and allowing Daiichi to withdraw the amount in deposit. Reproduces SEBI's interim order of 17 October 2018 and its final adjudication order of 19 April 2022 in the Fortis Healthcare matter, including the full lists of noticees. Neither list includes Gurinder Singh Dhillon or any member of his family; the word "Dhillon" does not appear in the judgment. Shivi Holdings Private Limited and RHC Holding Private Limited are noticees, penalised Rs 2.5 crore each in the 2022 order.

sources.title: Daiichi Sankyo Company Ltd v. Malvinder Mohan Singh and others, O.M.P.(EFA)(COMM.) 6/2016 with E.A. 625/2020, 668/2020 and 815/2020
sources.publisher: High Court of Delhi via Indian Kanoon
sources.note: Order of Justice Rekha Palli in the execution proceedings. Reproduces the status quo order of 19 February 2018 and the order of 26 February 2018 whose paragraph 5 records a garnishee order under Order 21 Rule 46A of the Code of Civil Procedure in respect of debts due to judgment debtors 14 and 19, Oscar Investments Ltd and RHC Holding Private Ltd, as listed in their affidavit of 2 December 2016. This establishes the garnishee proceedings and the provision under which they were taken; it does not itself name any member of the Dhillon family, who are identified as garnishees in the reporting at gsd-src-05, gsd-src-06 and gsd-src-08.

sources.title: Daiichi Sankyo Company Ltd v. Malvinder Mohan Singh and others, O.M.P.(EFA)(COMM.) 6/2016, order on EX.APPL.(OS) 3764/2022, 1615/2025 and 3763/2022
sources.publisher: High Court of Delhi via Indian Kanoon
sources.note: Order of Justice Subramonium Prasad appointing a forensic auditor to reconstruct the dissipation of Fortis Healthcare shares from 24 May 2016, to report within six months, with the matter listed on 1 April 2027. In 213 pages the only mention of any Dhillon is in the list of dates, recording that the Master Purchase Agreement of 12 February 2018 was endorsed by Gurpreet Singh Dhillon on behalf of RHT. The word "garnishee" does not appear in the order and no application concerning the Dhillon family is listed as pending.

sources.title: Daiichi Sankyo vs Singh Bros: Delhi HC directs former Religare Chief, Radha Soami head to pay up
sources.note: Reports that the Delhi High Court "has directed fifty-five garnishee parties to deposit the amount due to Malvinder and Shivinder Singh's RHC Holding with the Registrar General of the Court in connection with the ongoing execution proceedings in the Daiichi Sankyo arbitration case", and tags Gurinder Singh Dhillon and Radha Soami Satsang Beas among the parties. The order itself is not attached to the report and its text could not be obtained.

sources.title: Daiichi Sankyo case: Delhi High Court directs Dhillon family to submit their income proofs within four weeks
sources.note: Reports the Delhi High Court's direction that garnishees disputing liability file income tax returns, bank statements and balance sheets within four weeks showing how the transactions were reflected in their returns.

sources.title: Daiichi-Ranbaxy case: Delhi Police summons Radha Soami Satsang chief Gurinder Singh Dhillon
sources.note: Reports that Gurinder Singh Dhillon and family members were named in the first information report registered by the Economic Offences Wing of the Delhi Police on the complaint of Religare Finvest Ltd, and that a summons dated 26 August 2020 sought an explanation of funds transferred to his and his late wife's personal accounts. No copy of the FIR or summons, and no statement of the Delhi Police, could be obtained; the report is the only source for this.

sources.title: Don't owe any money to Singh Brothers' Company: Radha Soami Chief tells High Court
sources.note: Agency report of the application filed by Gurinder Singh Dhillon and his family in the Delhi High Court on 11 October 2019 stating that they do not owe money to RHC Holding and that RHC Holding had made false claims; Justice J.R. Midha sought responses from RHC Holding, the Singh brothers and Daiichi. Also records that the September 2019 order required the 55 garnishees, "including Dhillon family", to deposit the sums owed to RHC Holding with the Registrar General within 30 days.

sources.title: Baba Gurmeet Singh @ Maharaj Gurmeet Singh @ Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh v. Central Bureau of Investigation, CRA-D-240-D-2019 and connected appeals
sources.publisher: Punjab and Haryana High Court (judgment copy hosted by Verdictum)
sources.note: 113-page judgment of Chief Justice Sheel Nagu and Justice Vikram Aggarwal. Recites the trial court's judgment of conviction dated 11.01.2019 and order of sentence dated 17.01.2019 (life imprisonment and Rs 50,000 fine under s.120-B read with s.302 IPC for A1), FIR No. 685 of 2002 PS City Sirsa, CBI case RC10/3, the High Court's 10.11.2003 transfer of the investigation to the CBI, and that A1 "had been convicted on 25.08.2017 in a rape case" (RC-5). Operative part at para 204 acquits A1 and dismisses the appeals of Kuldeep Singh, Nirmal Singh and Krishan Lal (through legal representatives). Also refers to the pending castration case. Indian Kanoon copy is at https://indiankanoon.org/doc/81005547/ (not fetchable at time of research).

sources.title: Children of ISKCON v. ISKCON, No. 3:00-cv-01254 (N.D. Tex.)
sources.publisher: United States District Court for the Northern District of Texas (PACER via CourtListener/RECAP)
sources.note: Federal docket. Filed 12 June 2000 before Judge Sam A. Lindsay; named defendants include the International Society for Krishna Consciousness, ISKCON of California, ISKCON of San Diego, ISKCON of Southern California, ISKCON of Los Angeles, ISKCON of Port Royal, ISKCON of West Virginia, ISKCON Foundation, New Vrindaban Community, JAGA Inc, William Deadwyler II, Faramarz Attar, William Ogle and Keith Ham, among others. The order of 28 September 2001 (entered on the docket, copies to counsel 1 October 2001) grants the defendants' motions to dismiss; the judgment entered 30 November 2001 states that "plaintiffs's RICO claims against dfts International Society for Krishna Consciousness ... are dismissed with prejudice and plaintiffs' state law claims against these dfts are dismissed without prejudice." Case terminated 28 November 2001.

sources.title: Isha Foundation vs S. Kamaraj on 18 October, 2024 (SLP(Crl) No. 13992/2024)
sources.publisher: Supreme Court of India (Indian Kanoon copy)
sources.note: Order of the Chief Justice of India (D.Y. Chandrachud), J.B. Pardiwala and Manoj Misra JJ. Reproduces in full the Court's earlier order of 3 October 2024 (recording the in-chambers interaction with "Maa Mathi" and "Maa Maayu", i.e. Geeta Kamaraj and Latha Kamaraj, their statements that they joined the ashram at 24 and 27, are now 39 and 42, travel freely, one ran a 10km marathon, and that parents visit periodically; transfer of HCP No. 2487/2024 to the Supreme Court; stay of further police action). Records the Coimbatore Superintendent of Police's status report, including Isha Foundation's submissions on the FIRs arising from the 14 June 2024 confrontation and the fasting episode. Holds that the purpose of the habeas corpus petition was fulfilled, that the High Court's jurisdiction under Article 226 in a habeas corpus matter is "well-defined" and it was "unnecessary" to expand its ambit, closes HCP No. 2487/2024, and clarifies that closure does not affect other regulatory compliances required of Isha Foundation.

sources.title: SC dismisses the habeas corpus petition against Sadhguru's Isha Foundation

sources.title: Isha Foundation vs Union Of India and Others on 14 December, 2022 (W.P. No. 467 of 2022)
sources.note: Judgment of T. Raja, Acting Chief Justice, and D. Krishnakumar J. Isha Foundation challenged a show cause notice dated 19.11.2021 (Proc. No. DEE/TNPCS/CBS/F.CBS-NA/R/L/EC/2021) from the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board alleging construction at the Velliangiri Yoga Center between 2006 and 2014 without environmental clearance. The Court holds the Isha Yoga Center - 1,25,800.41 sq.m. built up on a 4,87,418.59 sq.m. plot, comprising residential units, a school and a meditation hall - falls within the definition of "educational institution" under the 22.12.2014 EIA Notification amendment, entitling it to exemption from environmental clearance for both pre-2006 and 2006-2014 construction, and quashes the show cause notice; no order as to costs.

sources.title: Supreme Court Upholds High Court's Order Quashing TN Pollution Control Board's Notice Against Isha Foundation

Kotiswar Singh JJ declining to interfere with the Madras High Court's 14 December 2022 ruling, on condition that no coercive action be taken but Isha Foundation maintain compliance with environmental norms; the Court said the ruling was not a "permanent gate pass" for irregular construction and required prior authorisation for future expansion.

sources.title: Madras High Court Orders Action Against Constructions By Isha Foundation In Coimbatore Village If Found To Be Unauthorised
sources.note: Reports the order of Chief Justice S.V. Gangapurwala and P.D. Audikesavalu J. in Vellingiri Hill Tribal Protection Society v. Union of India and Others (2023 LiveLaw (Mad) 241), a PIL filed by P. Muthammal alleging unapproved construction of the Adiyogi statue, an arch, a road, a parking lot and mandapams since 2016; directs the Joint Director of Town and Country Planning to verify whether necessary permissions were obtained and take expeditious action if the buildings do not conform to plan.

sources.title: High Court Ends Controversy: Rules in Favor of Isha Yoga Center

sources.title: Vellingiri Hill Tribal Protection Society v. Union of India and Others, W.P. No. 3556 of 2017 (order of 18 August 2023)
sources.publisher: Madras High Court (order copy hosted by LiveLaw)
sources.note: Order of Chief Justice Sanjay V. Gangapurwala and P.D. Audikesavalu J. The petition, filed by P. Muthammal for the Society, sought a writ of mandamus directing restoration of wetlands by demolishing unauthorised construction by Isha Foundation (respondent 12) on named survey fields at Ikkarai Poluvampatti village, Perur taluk, Coimbatore. The Special Government Pleader placed on record a status report that no-objection certificates and permissions had not been obtained by Isha Foundation. The Court directed the Joint Director, District Town and Country Planning, to verify the permissions in force after considering documents from both sides and, if not in order, to take expeditious steps regarding any building not constructed in accordance with the sanctioned plan and NOC; Isha Foundation was directed to place its documents before the authority within two weeks. The writ petition was disposed of with no order as to costs.

sources.title: Shankaracharya Jayendra Saraswathi Overcame Ordeal Of Sankaraman Murder Charge In 2013
sources.note: Gives the arrest date (11 November 2004), the sections invoked (IPC 120-B and 302), the bail dates for both seers, the Supreme Court transfer of the case to Puducherry, and names the trial judge who delivered the November 2013 acquittal, C.S. Murugan, Principal District and Sessions Judge, Puducherry, noting 24 original accused of whom one (Kathiravan) was killed in early 2013 before the verdict.

sources.title: Chronology of events in Sankararaman case
sources.note: Chronology confirming the murder date (3 September 2004), Jayendra Saraswathi's arrest on 11 November 2004, remand on 12 November 2004, the chargesheet filed by the Tamil Nadu police SIT on 21 January 2005, and bail for Vijayendra Saraswathi from the Madras High Court on 10 February 2005.

sources.title: Raids lead to Rs 409 crore unaccounted cash receipts: Tax dept
sources.note: Reports the Income Tax department's own release on searches of premises of a group of trusts and companies founded by "Kalki Bhagwan" at Varadaiahpalem, Chennai and Bengaluru, begun on Wednesday 16 October 2019; quotes the release estimating unaccounted cash receipts at about Rs 409 crore from FY 2014-15 onward from suppressed receipts and undocumented cash on property sales. The department did not name Kalki Bhagwan directly, describing him only as a spiritual guru associated with "oneness".

sources.title: I-T raids on properties of self-styled godman 'Kalki Bhagwan' in AP, Tamil Nadu
sources.note: Reports simultaneous Income Tax raids on 16 October 2019 at Kalki Bhagwan's ashram at Varadaiahpalem and premises in Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, and at the house and offices of his son Krishna in Hyderabad; documents and phones seized; officials examined foreign-donation and tax-evasion allegations.

sources.title: Kalki Bhagwan in soup as I-T dept alleges tax evasion
sources.note: Cites unnamed I-T department sources putting evaded tax at about Rs 500 crore; reports seizure of Rs 43.9 crore in Indian currency, US$ equivalent to about Rs 18 crore, and 88 kg of gold valued at about Rs 26 crore; carries the ashram's own statement responding to the raids.

sources.title: The rise of 'Kalki' Bhagwan: From an LIC agent to a self-proclaimed avatar
sources.note: Background profile; records a 2008 stampede at Oneness University premises; a 2010 allegation that Vijay Kumar had encroached forest and private land near the university; and a 2003 allegation that his son Krishna diverted funds from tax-exempt ashrams into a Los Angeles real-estate business. No court or official record of prosecution on any of these is cited in the article or located elsewhere.

sources.title: Sri Sathya Sai Loka Seva Trust vs Sri Sathya Sai Central Trust, R.S.A. No. 140 of 2019 (DEC)
sources.publisher: Karnataka High Court (hosted by Indian Kanoon)
sources.note: Justice R. Nataraj. Second appeal by the Sri Sathya Sai Loka Seva Trust and Muddenahalli trustees (including U. Gangadhara Bhat, S.S. Naganand, K. Sanjiva Shetty, B. Narayana Rao) against a first-appellate order that had let a suit (O.S. No.141/2015, Chikkaballapur) by Sri Sathya Sai Central Trust and its aligned trustees proceed. The suit challenges a 12 September 2012 amendment to the Loka Seva Trust's deed that removed the Central Trust's power, under the deed as it stood after Sathya Sai Baba's death, to nominate Loka Seva Trust trustees. Held the suit was properly filed to vindicate the plaintiffs' personal right to appoint trustees, not a public-trust matter requiring leave under CPC s.92; dismissed the second appeal as lacking merit.

sources.title: Sri Sathya Sai Lok Sewa Trust vs Sri Sathya Sai Central Trust, SLP (Civil) Diary No. 26627/2022 (order of 15 September 2023)
sources.publisher: Supreme Court of India (hosted by Indian Kanoon)
sources.note: Justices A.S. Bopanna and Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha. Special Leave Petition against the 19 April 2022 Karnataka High Court order (ms-src-01). "We see no reason to interfere in the petition under Article 136... The special leave petition stands disposed of," while leaving all contentions open to be raised in the written statement before the trial court.

sources.title: Sri Sathya Sai Lok Sewa Trust vs Sri Sathya Sai Central Trust, SLP (Civil) Diary No. 26627/2022 (order of 6 September 2023)
sources.publisher: Supreme Court of India (hosted by Indian Kanoon)
sources.note: Justices A.S. Bopanna and M.M. Sundresh. Earlier hearing in the same SLP, listing the matter for the following week.

sources.title: K.S. Krishna Bhat and others vs B. Narayan Rao and others, Writ Petition under Article 227 (order of 21 March 2022)
sources.publisher: Karnataka High Court (hosted by Indian Kanoon)
sources.note: Names Madhusudan Naidu (defendant no.7, then aged about 42) among the defendants. Records that the plaintiffs' O.S. No.12/2017 before the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Bantwal seeks a declaration and permanent injunction against the defendants "from interfering with the Management of Shri Sathya Sai Loka Seva Trust, Alike and Muddenahalli Campus". Dismissed the plaintiffs' challenge to a trial-court order that had allowed the defendants to file a belated written statement (with a cost of Rs 5,000).

sources.title: B. Narayana Rao and others vs K.S. Krishna Bhat and others, Civil Petition Nos. 472 of 2022 and 351 of 2024 (order of 21 October 2024)
sources.publisher: Karnataka High Court (hosted by Indian Kanoon)
sources.note: Justice N.S. Sanjay Gowda. Names Madhusudan Naidu (then aged about 43-44) among the Muddenahalli-side petitioners/respondents. Records that O.S. No.838/2017 (Bengaluru, filed by S.S. Naganand) and O.S. No.12/2017 (Bantwal, filed by K.S. Krishna Bhat and others) both seek a declaration that a Board of Trustees resolution passed on 21-23 January 2017 at Muddenahalli, removing the plaintiffs as trustees, was illegal, null and void. Dismissed the Muddenahalli side's petition to transfer O.S. No.838/2017 to Bangalore (CP 472/2022) and allowed Naganand's petition to transfer it to Bantwal instead (CP 351/2024), directing the two suits be tried together at Bantwal; both suits remain pending on their merits.

sources.title: Watch: PM Modi inaugurates free-of-cost medical college & hospital in Karnataka, pays tributes to Sir M V
sources.note: PTI wire report. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Sri Madhusudan Sai Institute of Medical Sciences and Research (SMSIMSR) and the Sri Sathya Sai Rajeswari Memorial Block, a fee-free medical college and hospital established by the Sri Sathya Sai University for Human Excellence, at Sathya Sai Grama, Muddenahalli, on 25 March 2023; Karnataka Chief Minister Basavaraj Bommai accompanied him.

sources.title: Chhattisgarh CM Vishnu Deo Sai visits Sathya Sai Grama in Karnataka, praises healthcare facilities and service initiatives
sources.note: Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai toured the Sri Sathya Sai Institute of Higher Medical Sciences (Super Speciality Hospital) at Sathya Sai Grama on 24 July 2026 and reviewed the free healthcare services provided there.

sources.title: Prakash and another v. Vandana and State of Kerala, Crl.M.C. No. 415 of 2015
sources.publisher: High Court of Kerala via Indian Kanoon
sources.note: Order of Justice P.V. Kunhikrishnan quashing C.C. No. 1618 of 2014 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate I, Karunagappally, a private complaint under IPC 499 and 500 by Vandana, a devotee, against the executive editor and the director and chief editor of Reporter Channel over the programme "Big Story" aired on 18 February 2014. The Court examined the English and Malayalam editions of the book, recording that Gail Tredwell published "Holy Hell" in 2013 through Wattle Tree Press, Maui, Hawaii, that the Malayalam translation "Vishudha Narakam" was published by Mythri Books, Thiruvananthapuram, in April 2014, that "there are serious allegations against Mata Amritanandamayi and the Math" in the book, and that "it is not clear whether any complaint is filed by Mata Amritanandamayi Math against the author of the book 'Holy Hell'". Held that discussing a book already in the public domain is "fair comment or criticisms which is part of their freedom of speech".

sources.title: Dr. Sreejith Krishnan and another v. Ravi D.C. and others, O.P.(C) No. 1038 of 2014
sources.publisher: High Court of Kerala via Indian Kanoon
sources.note: Judgment of Justice V. Chitambaresh. Two petitioners describing themselves as disciples had sued in the Sub Court, Thiruvalla for a permanent prohibitory injunction restraining D.C. Books, its group companies and John Brittas of Malayala Communication Ltd (Kairali and People TV) "from publishing, selling, circulating or distributing the book - Amruthananda Matdom - The revelations of a saintly lady - through out Kerala"; the Amruthanandamayi Math, Paryakadavu, is the sixth respondent. The High Court set aside the Sub Court's order of 2 April 2014 on court-fee valuation, directed the suit to be numbered and the temporary injunction application to be heard within a month, and directed that the interim order of 8 April 2014 "will govern the field" until then. The outcome of the suit is not on any record found. Indian Kanoon labels this document 2 April 2014; the judgment itself is dated 24 June 2014.

sources.title: Abad Builders Private Limited and connected cases v. State of Kerala, W.P.(C) No. 2785 of 2021 and connected cases (including W.P.(C) No. 2505 of 2024, Mata Amritanandamayi Math), Neutral Citation 2025:KER:999
sources.publisher: High Court of Kerala via Indian Kanoon
sources.note: Judgment of Justice Mohammed Nias C.P. in a batch of about 110 writ petitions. The Mata Amritanandamayi Math, represented by its general secretary Sreevalsan K. of Amritapuri P.O., Parayakadavu, Alappad, Kollam, is the petitioner in W.P.(C) No. 2505 of 2024. The Court declared "that Note 1 to Rule 12(9) is ultra vires the Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland Act, 2008 and Rules and the Amendment Act, 2018 to the extent it imposes a levy of fee of Rs.100/- per sq. feet exceeding 3000 sq. ft.", directed that no such demand be made against the petitioners and that amounts collected be refunded within four months, and allowed the writ petitions.

sources.title: Rationalist association leader to be prosecuted
sources.note: Reports that the Kerala government sanctioned the prosecution of Sreeni Pattathanam, general secretary of the Bharatiya Rationalists Association, and two others over the book "Mata Amritanandamayi: Divyakathakalum Yatharthyangalum", by an order of the Home Department under G.O. number 211/04 dated 20 January 2004, sent to Pattathanam, P.S. Kumar, owner of the publishing company, and S. Saji, the printer.

sources.title: Move to prosecute rationalist leader criticised
sources.note: Records that the sanction "followed directions from the High Court to the Home Department for considering an application by an inmate of the Mata Amritanandamayi Ashramam, T.K. Ajan, to prosecute the three", and carries the protest of the CPI leader Thengamam Balakrishnan.

sources.title: Indian Kanoon search for "Gail Tredwell"
sources.note: Two documents only: the Kerala High Court order of 19 July 2024 quashing the Reporter Channel defamation complaint, and the Kerala High Court judgment in O.P.(C) 1038 of 2014.

sources.title: Indian Kanoon search for "Amritanandamayi"
sources.note: The first page of results consists of the connected Kerala High Court writ petitions decided on 9 January 2025 in which the Mata Amritanandamayi Math is a petitioner. No criminal proceeding against Amritanandamayi or the Math appears.

sources.title: Indian Kanoon search for "Sreeni Pattathanam"
sources.note: Five results. The only Pattathanam matter is a 2011 Kerala High Court writ petition about the Makarajyothi at Sabarimala, unrelated to the Math. No judgment in the prosecution sanctioned in 2004 appears on the site.

sources.title: Indian Kanoon search for "Satnam Singh Amritanandamayi"
sources.note: No matching results.

sources.title: Amritanandamayi mutt row: Gail Tredwell, five news organisations booked
sources.note: Reports that Palarivattom police booked Gail Tredwell, the television channels Indiavision, Reporter and Mediaone and the newspapers Thejas and Madhyamam under IPC 153A, 153B, 295A, 298, 120B and 34, on a complaint by Cijith of Mamamangalam, after the Ernakulam judicial first class magistrate court ordered a case. Records that the same petition also targeted the person who had complained to the Karunagappally police seeking a probe into the book's allegations.

sources.title: Book on Amma: petition against media organisations, others
sources.note: Reports the private petition filed before the Ernakulam magistrate court. Quotes R. Krishna Raj, counsel for the petitioner Cijith, that the media organisations propagated the book's allegations "without verifying them, with the intent of communal polarisation". Records that the petition also raised charges against the person who had asked the Karunagappally police to investigate the allegations in the book.

sources.title: Amma's ex-aide alleges sexual abuse at ashram
sources.note: First major report on the memoir. The ashram representative Sudeep Kumar said the contents of the book "were absolutely baseless".

sources.title: Amma denies charges, Chandy backs her but Pinarayi seeks probe
sources.note: Amritanandamayi told a spiritual session in Palakkad that "her ashram was an open book and there was no lapse on its part", said "Some people are saying certain things against the ashram when their plans did not materialise. I am trying to forget and forgive these issues", and said the controversy was part of an attempt to trigger communal tension. Chief Minister Oommen Chandy backed her; the CPI(M) state secretary Pinarayi Vijayan sought a probe.

sources.title: CPM-backed Kairali TV airs interview of author who alleged sex abuse at Amritanandamayi ashram
sources.publisher: The Indian Express (Express News Service, Thiruvananthapuram)
sources.note: Records that a Delhi-based legal house served notice on Kairali TV to stop telecasting its interview with Tredwell and that the channel aired a second episode anyway. The ashram spokesman Raju Swami said the Math was not involved in serving the notice: "The stated notice might have been issued at the intervention of ashram devotees in Delhi. Amma has asked the devotees to refrain from such action."

sources.title: High Court notice to Kerala govt, CBI in Amritanadamayi mutt case
sources.note: Reports that on 14 March 2014 the Kerala High Court issued notices to the state government and the Central Bureau of Investigation on a writ petition under Article 226 by the Supreme Court lawyer Deepak Prakash, who said the Karunagappally police had declined to register a case on the allegations in the book and relied on Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh. The petition also sought a CBI probe. No outcome of the petition is on any record found.

sources.title: Amritanandamayi Math accused of assaulting spiritual leader and publisher
sources.note: Reports the 1 April 2014 assault on Swami Sandeepananda Giri at Tirur, in which five men described as RSS workers were arrested, and the stoning of the home of Ravi DeeCee of D.C. Books, which had published the Malayalam translation. "The MAM denied any involvement in both the incidents."

sources.title: Book publisher comes under attack in Kerala
sources.note: Reports that miscreants stormed the D.C. Books Heritage Centre at Kottayam and that stones were thrown at the home of Ravi DeeCee; a police case was registered.

sources.title: PCI plea to withdraw case
sources.note: The Press Club of India, through its president Anand Sahay, asked the Kerala government to withdraw the case registered against the news organisations.

sources.title: Police file case as controversy over 'hugging saint' rages
sources.note: Reports that a case was registered under the Information Technology Act at Karunagappally over social-media posts about the book, and carries the Kerala Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala's position on the limits of police action.

sources.title: Media entitled to discuss book available in public domain, Kerala High Court quashes criminal defamation case over book talk
sources.note: Report of the Kerala High Court order of 19 July 2024 quashing the Reporter Channel defamation case.

sources.title: Narayan @ Narayan Sai @ Mota Bhagwan v. State of Gujarat, Criminal Misc. Application (for suspension of sentence) No. 4 of 2025 in R/Criminal Appeal No. 1756 of 2019, order dated 4 May 2026
sources.publisher: Gujarat High Court (order PDF hosted by LiveLaw)
sources.note: Justices Ilesh J. Vora and R.T. Vachhani. Para 3 recites the trial by the 2nd Additional Sessions Judge, Surat in Sessions Case No. 141 of 2014, the judgment dated 30.04.2019 and the sentences under IPC 376(2)(c), 377, 354, 504, 506(2), 508 and 323. Records that this was the fifth successive application and lists the earlier ones.

sources.title: Narayan @ Narayan Sai @ Mota Bhagwan v. State of Gujarat, R/Special Criminal Application (furlough leave) No. 6111 of 2025, order dated 30 April 2025 (2025:GUJHC:24733)
sources.publisher: Gujarat High Court (order PDF hosted by LiveLaw)
sources.note: Justice M.R. Mengdey. Records that he has been lodged in jail since 04.12.2013, the conviction and total fine of Rs 2,40,500, offences registered against his disciples for threatening or assaulting witnesses, his attempt to bribe government officials, and jail punishments.

sources.title: 'Prima Facie Adopted Delay Tactics': Gujarat High Court Refuses To Suspend Narayan Sai's Life Sentence In Rape Case
Supreme Court Refuses To Suspend Sentence Of Asaram's Son Narayan Sai In 2013 Rape Case
sources.note: Diary No. 29992-2026; names the trial judge as Additional Sessions Judge P.S. Gadhvi and gives the co-accused sentences.

sources.title: Supreme Court refuses to suspend jail sentence of Asaram Bapu's son Narayan Sai in rape case
Gujarat Court sentences Asaram's son Narayan Sai to life imprisonment for rape of disciple
sources.note: Reports the guilty finding on 26 April 2019 and sentence on 30 April 2019, fine of Rs 1 lakh and compensation of Rs 5 lakh, co-accused sentences, and arrest in December 2013 at the Delhi-Haryana border. Its list of IPC sections differs from the High Court's recital.

sources.title: Surat Rape Case | 'Contradictions In Victim's Testimony': Narayan Sai Tells Gujarat High Court In Bail Plea
sources.note: Appeal R/CR.A/1756/2019; hearing of 17 March 2026 before Justices Ilesh J. Vora and R.T. Vachhani.

sources.title: Gujarat High Court Declines Narayan Sai's Furlough Plea In 2014 Surat Rape Case
Nirmaljit Singh Narula @ Nirmal Baba vs State Of Bihar & Anr on 22 June, 2017
sources.publisher: Patna High Court (copy hosted by Indian Kanoon)
sources.note: Criminal Miscellaneous No.32693 of 2013, Arun Kumar J. Quashes the order dated 09.07.2013 of the Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Muzaffarpur, taking cognizance under IPC 417 and 298 against Nirmal Baba in Complaint Case No.955 of 2012 filed by Sudhir Kumar Ojha, holding there was no material to take cognizance even on the uncontroverted allegations.

sources.title: FIR against Nirmal Baba for cheating, fraud
sources.note: Reports that Chief Judicial Magistrate Rajesh Upadhyaya, Lucknow, on 9 May 2012 directed Gomti Nagar police station to register a case against Nirmal Baba on a complaint by two siblings; quotes the magistrate's order describing his "samagam" solutions as superstition and cheating. Later outcome of this case not located.

sources.title: Godman Nirmal Baba likely to be arrested on Apr 23
sources.note: Reports an FIR filed against Nirmal Baba in Bihar on 22 April 2012 and that police sought an arrest warrant; states he had been "booked in different cheating and forgery cases in many states."

sources.title: Rs 3.5-cr service tax evasion charge against 'Nirmal Baba'
sources.note: Reports a Rs 3.58-crore service-tax demand raised by the Directorate General of Central Excise Intelligence since July 2012 over "Daswand" donations, which Nirmal Baba was contesting, in addition to an already-paid demand of about Rs 3.08 crore plus Rs 80 lakh interest on entry fees to his "Samagam" events.

sources.title: Nithyananda Swamy formerly known as Sri Thiru Rajashekarem vs The State of Karnataka, Crl.P. No. 2328/2010 (with 2329 and 2344/2010)
sources.publisher: Karnataka High Court via Indian Kanoon
sources.note: Bail order. Records Crime Nos. 141/2010 and 142/2010, Bidadi PS (transferred from CCB Chennai Crime No. 112/2010), IPC 295A, 376, 377, 420, 506(1), 120B; petitioner arrested outside Karnataka; bail on Rs 1,00,000 bond with conditions.

sources.title: Sri Paramahamsa Nithyananda vs State of Karnataka, Crl.P. Nos. 6920/2018 and 6927/2018
sources.publisher: Karnataka High Court via Indian Kanoon
sources.note: Sets aside the trial court's order of 06.09.2018 in S.C. No. 86/2014 (III Addl. District & Sessions Judge, Ramanagara) rejecting exemption applications and issuing non-bailable warrants against accused 1 and 3; "shall not preclude the learned Sessions Judge from directing the presence of the accused on future dates".

sources.title: K. Lenin vs Nithyananda Swamy and State of Karnataka, Crl.P. No. 594/2020
sources.publisher: Karnataka High Court via Indian Kanoon
sources.note: Cancels the bail granted on 11.06.2010; records that the accused has not appeared before the trial court since 05.06.2018, that his whereabouts are unknown to the prosecution and to the ashram in-charge, that his passport expired on 30.09.2018, and that he "has run away to a foreign country to escape the trial"; directs the trial court to take custody and enforce the bonds.

sources.title: Janardhana Ramkrishna Sharma vs State of Gujarat, R/SCR.A/9973/2019
sources.publisher: Gujarat High Court via Indian Kanoon
sources.note: Habeas corpus petition dismissed; records FIR C.R. No. I-138 of 2019, Vivekanand police station (Hathijan, Ahmedabad Rural), registered 17 November 2019, arising from the Yogini Sarvagyapeetham facility affiliated to Nithyananda Dhyanpeetham; the two adult daughters (21 and 18) told the court by video link that they left India of their own free will.

sources.title: Sri Nithyananda Swami vs The Commissioner, HR&CE, W.P. No. 21276 of 2017
sources.publisher: Madras High Court via Indian Kanoon
sources.note: Writ petition by the founder of Nithyananda Dhyanapeetam, Bidadi, against the HR&CE Commissioner's order of 22.06.2017 appointing an Executive Officer to administer mutt properties under s.60 of the HR&CE Act, dismissed; the court records that "the whereabouts of the 1st petitioner is now not known" and that the nomination in his favour was invalid.

sources.title: Karnataka trial court frames charges against Nithyananda in rape case
sources.note: Charges framed 6 June 2018 by the III Additional District and Sessions Court, Ramanagara under IPC 376, 377, 420, 114, 201, 120B; names co-accused A2 to A6.

sources.title: Rape case against Nithyananda: Trial court issues non-bailable warrant for him
sources.note: NBW of 6 September 2018 for absence since 6 June 2018 and non-compliance with counsel's undertaking.

sources.title: 'No more delays': SC asks trial court to frame charges against Nithyananda
sources.note: Supreme Court direction of 6 December 2017 that the Ramanagara sessions court proceed to frame charges, considering only the prosecution's chargesheet documents at that stage. The order text itself was not located on Indian Kanoon.

sources.title: Rape case against Nithyananda: Trial finally begins after 8 years of legal hurdles
sources.note: Witness examination began 8 August 2018 in his absence.

sources.title: Nithyananda rape case: Karnataka HC stays proceedings of Ramanagara sessions court
sources.note: Justice G. Narendar stayed the trial court proceedings on 13 December 2019 on the complainant's petition and called for the records.

sources.title: HC rejects whistleblower's plea to transfer Nithyananda rape case out of Ramanagara
sources.note: Justice B.A. Patil refused transfer and directed the trial court to expedite the trial.

sources.title: Karnataka: Court issues non-bailable warrant against Nithyananda
sources.note: III Additional District and Sessions Court, Ramanagara issued an NBW on 18 August 2022, returnable 23 September; three witnesses had been examined and the trial had stalled for about three years in the accused's absence.

sources.title: Nithyananda case: Police say religious leader fled abroad, MEA claims it has no formal information
sources.note: Ahmedabad (Rural) SP R.V. Asari said Nithyananda had fled abroad; two disciples (Pranpriyanand and Riddhi Kiran) arrested on 19 November 2019 and remanded to five days' police custody; Child Labour Act charges added.

sources.title: Interpol issues blue corner notice for Nithyananda on Gujarat Police's request
sources.note: Gujarat Police disclosed the claimed Blue Corner notice in a chargesheet filed in a local court; the chargesheet recorded that Nithyananda had fled the country in November 2019.

sources.title: Interpol Issues Blue Corner Notice Against Absconding Rape Accused Nithyananda
sources.note: Deputy Superintendent of Police K.T. Kamariya (Ahmedabad Rural) quoted as saying Interpol issued the Blue Corner notice "this month".

sources.title: Nithyananda case: Interpol denies issuing Blue Corner notice for fugitive godman
sources.note: Two letters from Interpol's General Secretariat (26 February 2021 and 22 November 2022), obtained by journalist Poonam Joshi, state that "Nithyananda, also known as Swami Arunachalam Sri Nithyananda, is not subject to an Interpol Notice or diffusion as of November 2022". This contradicts the Gujarat Police statement of January 2020.

sources.title: Ecuador Says It Denied Nithyananda Asylum; MEA Says He Left India Without Passport
sources.note: MEA spokesperson Raveesh Kumar at the weekly briefing of 6 December 2019 - passport issued October 2008 cancelled before its September 2018 expiry, fresh application refused on adverse police report, missions abroad sensitised; Ecuador's embassy "categorically denies" granting asylum or helping him buy land. The MEA transcript itself could not be retrieved from mea.gov.in.

sources.title: Wanted Indian guru resurfaces to announce new 'cosmic' country
sources.note: Announcement of "Kailaasa" in December 2019; 2010 arrest and 53 days in jail; Gujarat officer quoted via PTI.

sources.title: Newark rescinds sister-city agreement entered into with 'United States of Kailasa', terms incident regrettable
sources.note: Ceremony 12 January 2023, rescinded 18 January 2023; Newark press secretary Susan Garofalo quoted - "Based on deception, the ceremony was groundless and void".

sources.title: City of Newark falls for Sister City scam: "Whose job was it to do a simple Google search?"
sources.note: Mayor Ras Baraka invited Kailasa representatives to City Hall; City Hall said no money changed hands and the ceremony was "groundless and void".

sources.title: UN dismisses 'irrelevant' submissions by fugitive Nithyananda's Kailasa at Geneva meetings
sources.note: OHCHR statement that Kailasa representatives attended two public meetings (22 and 24 February 2023, the latter CESCR) and that their submission "will not be taken into consideration by the Committee".

sources.title: Paraguay official sacked after dealings with fictitious country
sources.note: Arnaldo Chamorro, chief of staff to the agriculture minister, removed on 29 November 2023; the ministry said the memorandum "cannot be considered official".

sources.title: Destituyen al jefe de gabinete del MAG tras firmar acuerdo con Kailasa, país inexistente
sources.note: MAG Resolution 554 appointing an interim chief of staff; Kailasa representatives met MAG officials in October 2023.

sources.title: Bolivia expulsa a 20 extranjeros del Estado ficticio de Kailasa
sources.note: Dirección General de Migración ordered the "salida obligatoria" of 20 people (Chinese, Indian, Swedish, US, German, British, Portuguese) who had entered as tourists; lease documents for about 480,000 hectares with the Baure, Cayubaba and Esse Ejja peoples; complaints lodged with the Ministerio Público.

sources.title: Bolivia expels members of Kailasa over Indigenous land lease scandal
sources.note: Quotes Migración director Katherine Calderón, Minister of Rural Development Yamil Flores, and Beni prosecutor Gerardo Balderas (investigation for land trafficking and criminal organisation).

sources.title: Emisarios de Kailasa son expulsados en Bolivia por estafa
sources.note: Per-community figures - Baure 60,000 ha, Cayubaba 31,000 ha, Esse Ejja (TIM II) about 390,000 ha; Kailasa's social-media response calling the expulsion "hindufobia".

sources.title: 3 B.C. cities rescind recognition of 'great cosmic borderless nation'
sources.note: Surrey, Victoria and Nanaimo withdrew "Guru Purnima Day" proclamations issued at Kailasa's request; Surrey said the proclamation "was signed in error".

sources.title: The Press Secretary office of The Holy See of Hinduism responds to NBC News correspondent Valerie Castro's inquiry
sources.note: Subject's own statement; used only for response_from_subject.

sources.title: 'Borderless'... Not 'Fiction': Nithyananda's Office On Kailasa Amid 'Scam' Allegations
sources.note: Reports the organisation's statement that "Kailasa and its representatives have not scammed anyone, nor are we 'fiction'".

sources.title: Kailasa issues statement denying Nithyananda's death, says he is "safe and active"
sources.note: Organisation's April 2025 statement; also reports Bolivia's expulsion of 20 members.

sources.title: Swami Nithyananda booked, two disciples held for 'kidnapping' kids
sources.note: Supporting detail only - DSP K.T. Kamariya quoted; FIR sections IPC 365, 344, 323, 504 and Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act s.14.

sources.title: A Ramanagara District Court issues Non Bailable Warrant against self proclaimed Godman Nithyananda
sources.note: NBW of 19 February 2020 in Bidadi Police v. Paramahamsa Nithyanandaswamy @ Rajashekaran; "the personal bond executed by him stands forfeited".

sources.title: Bolivia inició deportaciones de miembros del estado ficticio de Kailasa
sources.note: Quotes regional Migración director Andrea Miranda ("contaban con documentos firmados de transferencias de tierras benianas, algo ilegal") and Minister Yamil Flores.

sources.title: Godman Nithyananda in trouble again
sources.note: Karnataka government ordered his arrest and the sealing of the Bidadi ashram in June 2012; Chief Minister D.V. Sadananda Gowda quoted.

sources.title: Fugitive self-styled godman Nithyananda's Ahmedabad ashram demolished

sources.title: Hat der Hessische Rundfunk ein Sorgfaltsproblem? (Pressemitteilung)
sources.publisher: Bhakti Marga / IRLE MOSER Rechtsanwälte (Dr Ben M. Irle)
sources.note: Press release by the community's lawyers. States that they obtained for Vishwananda and one further person, before the Landgericht Hamburg, Zivilkammer 24, "bislang sieben einstweilige Verfügungen" over the Hessischer Rundfunk television and podcast production "Just Love", and gives the case numbers 324 O 66/22, 324 O 67/22, 324 O 68/22, 324 O 69/22, 324 O 70/22, 324 O 71/22 and 324 O 119/22. States that no objection had been lodged at that date, and records that Der Spiegel and the Süddeutsche Zeitung had reported the matter. A party's account of court orders, not the orders themselves.

sources.title: Stellungnahme Bhakti Marga zur Berichterstattung des Hessischen Rundfunk
sources.note: The community's own statement, with a criminal-law annex dated 18 February 2022 by counsel Götz Buchheim. States that a lawyer instructed by Bhakti Marga obtained file inspection (Akteneinsicht) at the Staatsanwaltschaft Wiesbaden and that there had been "in den Jahren 2009 bis 2021 tatsächlich insgesamt sechs Ermittlungsverfahren" against Vishwananda arising from criminal complaints, all discontinued "in einem frühen Stadium … weil die Staatsanwaltschaft das Vorliegen eines hinreichenden Tatverdachts verneint hat". Also reproduces the correspondence between the broadcaster and IRLE MOSER, including an email of 23 December 2021 in which the hr editor Stefan Bücheler refers to "ihren Mandanten Mahadeosing Komalram". The linked annex PDF is a scan without a text layer.

sources.title: Stellungnahme "Just Love": Erfolge für den hr im Rechtsstreit gegen den Guru der Sekte Bhakti Marga
sources.note: The broadcaster's own account of the litigation. States that the hr was "vor dem Oberlandesgericht Hamburg zuletzt im Februar in der Auseinandersetzung über zwei Punkte im Podcast, bei denen wir in Berufung gegangen sind, vollständig erfolgreich"; that the court praised the podcast as reporting "ausgewogen und differenziert"; and that "Guru Vishwananda sei ausreichend konfrontiert worden zu den Vorwürfen". Records that the Landgericht Hamburg had prohibited various points in several preliminary injunctions, that the podcast is available only in shortened form and the film is offline, and that both sides filed sworn affidavits (eidesstattliche Versicherungen). The page has since been removed from the live site under the broadcaster's retention rules; the archived copy is authoritative.
