sources.title: Bhakti Marga (Lexikon-Eintrag)
sources.publisher: Relinfo, Evangelische Informationsstelle "Kirchliche Fachstelle Religionen, Sekten und Weltanschauungen", Zurich
sources.note: Swiss church-run research service. Reporting the hr investigation, it states that of the criminal complaints lodged with the Staatsanwaltschaft Wiesbaden "vier im Zusammenhang mit sexualisierter Gewalt stehen und eine Anzeige den Guru des mutmasslichen Totschlags bezichtigt", and that "Alle Ermittlungsverfahren wurden eingestellt". It also states that he was sentenced in Switzerland to four months suspended for property damage and disturbance of freedom of belief and worship over the opening of reliquaries in Catholic churches in 2001. Accounts of that Swiss case differ across sources as to the court, the year (2003, 2007 or a 2008 appeal) and the exact offences and sentence, and no judgment could be obtained: searches of entscheidsuche.ch, which indexes the Swiss Federal Supreme Court and the cantonal courts, returned nothing for Vishwananda, Komalram or Bhakti Marga. The Swiss sentence is therefore not entered as a case or claim in this file.

sources.note: Six dead (four women inside the complex, one woman and an 18-month-old child at hospital); hundreds injured; more than 40 summons ignored.

sources.title: Haryana Court Convicts Self-Styled Godman Rampal Dass in Two Murder Cases
sources.note: The Wire Staff. Conviction of 11 October 2018; 43 summons ignored before arrest; August 2017 acquittal in two cases; 22 months in custody after the 2006 case until 2008.

sources.title: 'Used Devotees As Human Shields To Resist Arrest': P&H High Court Denies Bail To Self-Styled Godman Rampal Accused Of Waging War Against India
sources.note: Report on CRM-M-15399-2021 (2023 LiveLaw (PH) 173).

sources.title: Punjab & Haryana HC Dismisses Bail Plea Of Self-Styled Godman Rampal [Read Order]
sources.note: CRM No. 14574/2020, Justices S. Muralidhar and Avneesh Jhingan, 7 July 2020; interim bail for granddaughter's wedding refused.

sources.title: Spent Over 10 Yrs In Jail: P&H High Court Suspends Life Sentence Of Self-Styled Godman Rampal, Tells Him To Refrain From 'Mob Mentality'
sources.note: Report on the 2 September 2025 order; links the order PDF (rampal-src-01).

sources.title: Punjab and Haryana High Court closes 2014 contempt of court case against Sant Rampal
sources.note: Contempt case closed on Wednesday 8 October 2025 after Rampal sought the court's forgiveness for the 2014 violence. Body of article is paywalled; the lede states the outcome.

sources.title: Punjab and Haryana High Court suspends sentence of godman Rampal in murder cases
sources.note: States that the life sentences in both murder cases were suspended. Body of article is paywalled; the lede states the outcome.

sources.title: Cop found at Satlok Ashram during police action sacked
sources.note: Criminal contempt proceedings before the High Court against Rampal, Ram Kumar Dhaka and Dr O.P. Hooda; 112 police personnel injured during the operation.

sources.title: Haryana page, 12 November 2014 (Satlok Ashram coverage)
sources.note: 2006 FIR of 12 July 2006 under IPC 148, 302, 323, 324, 307, 120-B and Arms Act 25; bail by High Court single bench on 2 April 2008; fresh non-bailable warrant on 5 November 2014.

sources.title: What type of murder cases is Sant Rampal Ji Maharaj accused of?
sources.note: The organisation's own account of the 2014 deaths; used only for the subject's response.

sources.title: Sant Rampal Ji's Bail in FIR 428 Signals Truth's Victory
sources.publisher: Jagat Guru Rampal Ji news site (organisation website)
sources.note: Organisation's account; gives 28 August 2025 as the date the sentence in FIR 430 was suspended and 2 September 2025 for FIR 429. Not relied on for any adverse claim.

sources.title: Punjab & Haryana High Court Closes Contempt Case Against 274 Followers Of Self-Styled Godman Rampal For Criticising Judge
sources.note: CROCP-4/2019, order of 7 November 2024, Justices Sureshwar Thakur and Sudeepti Sharma; followers who published a book criticising Judge D.R. Chalia discharged on unconditional apology.

sources.title: Santosh Kumar Roul v. State Of Orissa (BLAPL No. 3892 of 2019)
sources.note: Bail application under s.439 Cr.P.C. by Santosh Kumar Roul @ Sarathi Baba in CID, CB, Cuttack P.S. Case No. 20 of 2015 (G.R. Case No. 1062 of 2015, pending before the S.D.J.M., Kendrapara) for offences under IPC 120-B, 420, 354, 506 read with 34. Recites the FIR dated 20.08.2015 and its allegations of cheating, confinement, forced labour, threats with nude photographs and molestation; records that earlier bail applications before the High Court and the Supreme Court had been rejected; grants bail on the ground of prolonged undertrial detention under s.436-A Cr.P.C. Justice S.K. Sahoo.

sources.title: Charges Framed Against Sarathi Baba In 2015 Crime Branch Case
sources.note: Reports that a Special Court under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act (ADJ-3) at Cuttack framed charges against Sarathi Baba, alias Santosh Roul, in the Crime Branch case registered after his August 2015 arrest from his Kendrapara ashram, covering offences under the IPC, the Arms Act 1959 and the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989; says the case will move to trial.

sources.title: Obituary: Indian guru Sai Baba
sources.note: By Tanya Datta, who made the 2004 BBC documentary "Secret Swami". Records the 1993 killings, the Rahm family's on-camera sexual-abuse allegations, Michael Goldstein's denial on behalf of the organisation, and states Sai Baba "was never investigated on this issue" and "all attempts to prosecute him failed".

sources.title: Sathya Sai Baba
sources.note: Obituary. Records the 1993 assassination attempt (chauffeur and cook murdered, the four intruders shot dead by police), the long-running sexual-abuse allegations against young male devotees, an international campaign by devotees calling for his prosecution, and states he "was never investigated by the Indian authorities".

sources.title: Sai Baba, spiritual guru to millions, dies at 85
sources.note: By Jason Burke in Delhi. States Sai Baba "was never been charged with any offence over the sex abuse allegations and had denied all the charges against him"; quotes his 2000 denial to followers and quotes former devotee Barry Pittard's criticism; records that "In 1993, six people died violently in the spiritual leader's private rooms."

sources.title: This World: Secret Swami
sources.note: BBC's own programme page for "Secret Swami" (BBC Two, 17 June 2004, reporter Tanya Datta), which carried on-camera allegations from former devotee Alaya Rahm and his father Al Rahm that Sai Baba had sexually abused them during private interviews.

sources.title: Inside Sathya Sai Baba's fiefdom
sources.note: By Vishal Arora. Long-form investigation quoting Hari Sampath's 12 March 2001 affidavit to the CBI, and recording that "the petition of Indian-American ex-follower Hari Sampath was dismissed by Indian Supreme Court Justices GB Pattnaik and RC Lahoti on 8 May 2001" after the CBI did not respond to his complaint; also records Alaya Rahm's 2004 BBC allegations and a 2000 Daily Telegraph interview with Dr Naresh Bhatia.

sources.title: Rs 11.56cr cash, 98kg gold at Sai Baba's abode
sources.note: Reports that a 36-hour accounting since Yajur Mandir was opened on 16 June 2011 yielded 98 kg of gold (valued at Rs 20 crore), 307 kg of silver (Rs 1.6 crore) and Rs 11.56 crore in cash; quotes trust member R.J. Rathnakar that the cash was deposited in the trust's SBI account and that no will was found; records that the inventory was witnessed by retired Supreme Court judge A.P. Mishra, retired Karnataka HC judge Vaidyanathan and an income-tax department-approved assessor.

sources.title: Huge amount of gold, silver, cash found in Sai Baba's chamber
sources.note: Corroborates the 98 kg gold / 307 kg silver / Rs 11.56 crore cash figures from Yajur Mandir, opened the previous day.

sources.title: Sai Baba's personal chamber opened
sources.note: Same-day report that the Sathya Sai Central Trust opened Yajur Mandir, Sai Baba's personal chamber at Prasanthi Nilayam, on 16 June 2011.

sources.title: Assets worth Rs77L seized at Sai ashram
sources.note: A follow-up inspection by Anantapur district authorities of four further rooms in Yajur Mandir found gold, silver and a diamond ring worth Rs 76.89 lakh (116 kg silver worth Rs 56 lakh, 906 g gold worth Rs 15 lakh, a diamond ring worth Rs 3 lakh); quotes joint collector Anita Ramachandran; records that trust member V. Srinivasan had, days earlier, denied then admitted the trust's connection to the Rs 35.5 lakh cash seized from a vehicle, saying it was collected by R.J. Rathnakar from devotees to fund a "mahasamadhi" memorial and was being sent to a contractor.

sources.title: Three-day count at Baba's ashram yields treasure
sources.note: Reports the final inventory at Brindavan (the trust's Bangalore ashram, Whitefield): 6.09 kg of gold coins and jewellery, 245.368 kg of silver articles and Rs 80.5 lakh in cash; quotes trust media coordinator Prof A. Anantharaman that Rs 4.81 crore was paid in tax on the inventory and that the wealth-listing exercise concludes; names trustees present as Srinivasan, Naganand, Ratnakar and Bhagavan; conducted with Bangalore Urban deputy commissioner M.K. Aiyappa and police as independent witnesses.

sources.title: Seizure of cash: Sai Baba's nephew to be questioned
sources.note: PTI wire report. A vehicle carrying Rs 35.5 lakh in cash, said to belong to the Sai Central Trust, was confiscated at Kodikonda checkpost (Chilamanthur police station limits) on 18 June 2011; three men, including the vehicle's driver Harishnanda Shetty and trust member V. Srinivasan's driver Chandrashekhar, were arrested; Andhra Pradesh police issued notices calling trust member V. Srinivasan and Sai Baba's nephew R.J. Rathnakar for questioning.

sources.title: Sri Sathya Sai Central Trust, Bangalore vs Additional Director of Income Tax, ITA No. 1129/Bang/2017
sources.publisher: Income Tax Appellate Tribunal, Bangalore (hosted by Indian Kanoon)
sources.note: Bench of George George K (Judicial Member) and B.R. Baskaran (Accountant Member). Appeal by the trust (PAN AABTS4384C) against a CIT(A) order for assessment year 2011-12, concerning disallowance of a loss on sale of investments, capital gains on gifted assets, the deduction rate on net surplus, treatment of accumulated income and depreciation as application of income. The Tribunal held largely for the trust (Canara Bank bonds were an eligible investment; depreciation allowable as application of income per the Supreme Court's Rajasthan and Gujarati Charitable Foundation ruling), remanded some issues to the assessing officer, and treated the appeal "as allowed for statistical purposes".

sources.title: Enforcement Directorate vs Shiv Murat Diwedi Anr on 19 November, 2025
sources.note: SC No. 6594/2016, ECIR No. ECIR/53/DLZO/2010, Additional Sessions Judge Ravindra Kumar Pandey, South District, Saket Courts. Records that ED alleged Dwivedi and co-accused Praveen Kumar committed scheduled offences under ITPA ss.5, 6 and 8 (running a prostitution racket, 2001-2010, Delhi) and laundered the proceeds (Rs 90,74,132 deposited by Dwivedi, referencing FIR Nos. 47/2010 and 54/2010, PS Saket); charges under PMLA s.4 framed 14.05.2016; final order "Acquitted", holding the ED's investigating officer had not traced any money trail, verified the bank or property records, or established the alleged proceeds of crime.

sources.title: Shiv Murat Dwivedi vs Directorate Of Enforcement on 1 September, 2025
sources.note: W.P.(C) 6616/2025 and CM Appl.30082/2025, Justice Sachin Datta. A short listing order in a writ petition filed by Dwivedi against the Enforcement Directorate; confirms an active, separate challenge by Dwivedi to ED's conduct of the matter pending before the Delhi High Court in 2025.

sources.title: Shiva Sankaran @ Shiva Sankar Baba vs State Represented By on 7 December, 2021
sources.note: CRL.O.P.No.23835 of 2021, Justice M. Nirmal Kumar. Petition by Shiva Sankaran @ Shiva Shankar Baba to set aside a trial court search-warrant order in Crime No.10 of 2021 (CBCID, Metro Wing-II, Chennai). Records that earlier FIRs, Crime Nos. 1 and 3 of 2021, were registered by CB-CID, Kancheepuram against Sivasankar Baba and others; that in Crime No.3 of 2021 most co-accused were granted anticipatory bail during January-August 2021; that on completion of investigation three chargesheets were filed and taken on file as Special S.C. Nos. 69 to 71 of 2021; and identifies the petitioner as founder of Sushil Hari International School and the Ramarajiya Trust. Dismisses the petition and confirms the trial court's search-warrant order.

sources.title: #MeToo: Shiva Shankar Baba, who fled Chennai after sexual abuse charges at school, nabbed in Delhi
sources.note: Sahaya Novinston Lobo. Reports that Shiva Shankar Baba, founder of the Sushil Hari International Residential School at Kelambakkam, was arrested by the CB-CID in Delhi after absconding once his case was transferred from Chennai police to CB-CID; says three cases were registered against him under the IPC, POCSO Act and the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act, after school alumni alleged sexual abuse on social media.

sources.title: Shiva Shankar Baba remanded for sexually abusing minors
sources.note: Reports that Shiva Shankar Baba was produced before the magistrate at Chengalpattu and remanded to 15 days' judicial custody on 17 June 2021, after his arrest in Delhi by CB-CID the previous day; names Mahabalipuram All-Women Police as the registering authority.

sources.title: Madras High Court recalls order that quashed sexual harassment case against 'godman' Shiva Sankar Baba
sources.note: Ayesha Arvind. Reports that the Madras High Court, on 21 November 2022, recalled Justice R.N. Manjula's 17 October 2022 order which had quashed an FIR against Shiva Sankar Baba on the ground of a "technical flaw".

sources.title: Madras High Court says it would not have quashed sexual harassment FIR against Shiva Sankar Baba if it knew chargesheet was filed
sources.note: Ayesha Arvind. Reports that on 4 November 2022 the Madras High Court said it would not have quashed the sexual-harassment case against Shiva Sankar Baba on 17 October 2022 had it known a chargesheet had already been filed in the case.

sources.title: Aurangabad bench to hear PIL against Shirdi Trust's new panel
sources.note: Bombay High Court (bench headed by Justice V.M. Kanade) transferred to its Aurangabad bench a PIL challenging the state government's appointment of a new managing committee to run the Shirdi Sai Baba Trust, alleging appointees had political affiliations and criminal antecedents; clubbed with a similar pending matter at Aurangabad.

sources.title: Mumbai: HC restrains new committee of Shirdi temple trust from taking policy decisions
sources.note: Agencies. Aurangabad Bench (Justices R.V. Ghuge and S.G. Mehare) restrained the Maharashtra government's 16 September 2021 committee, headed by NCP MLA Ashutosh Kale, from taking policy decisions, sanctioning expenditure or making appointments. Records that a committee of the Ahmednagar principal district judge, district collector and Sansthan CEO had been appointed by the court in 2012, and that on 9 October 2019 the court had "empowered the Committee to administer the Sansthan"; petitioner Uttamrao Shelke's PIL on the trust's functioning is described as filed roughly ten years earlier.

sources.title: [Sai Baba Sansthan Trust] Appointment of trustees for public interest of devotees, not private interest of ruling party: Bombay High Court
sources.note: By Neha Joshi. Uttamrao Rambhaji Shelke & Ors. v. State of Maharashtra & Ors. and connected pleas; the Aurangabad Bench (Justices R.D. Dhanuka and S.G. Mehare) cancelled the September 2021 committee's appointment and directed the state to constitute a new committee within 8 weeks, holding that trustee appointments serve the public interest of devotees, not the ruling government's political interest.

sources.title: Search results: Uttamrao Rambhaji Shelke vs The State Of Maharashtra And Others
sources.publisher: Bombay High Court (indexed by Indian Kanoon)
sources.note: Indian Kanoon's index confirms the judgment "Uttamrao Rambhaji Shelke vs The State Of Maharashtra And Others on 13 September, 2022" (author R.D. Dhanuka; bench R.D. Dhanuka and S.G. Mehare; "ALONG WITH CIVIL APPLICATION NO.11973 OF 2021"), along with the same petitioner's earlier PIL No. 98 of 2021 (14 October 2021 order, bench Ghuge and Mehare) and PIL No. 120 of 2019 (9 October 2019 order, bench Varale and Gharote), corroborating the Bar & Bench and Free Press Journal reporting. The full text of the 13 September 2022 order could not be retrieved (Indian Kanoon's document view did not return the correct document on repeated attempts); this citation rests on the search index's excerpted text of the judgment together with the news reporting above.

sources.title: Bombay High Court rules Sai Baba Sansthan Trust eligible for Income Tax exemption on anonymous donations
sources.note: By Sahyaja MS. Commissioner of Income Tax v. Shree Sai Baba Sansthan Trust. The Bombay High Court (Justices G.S. Kulkarni and Somasekhar Sundaresan) upheld an ITAT order (25 October 2023) that Rs 159.12 crore in anonymous "hundi" donations received across assessment years 2015-16, 2017-18 and 2018-19 is exempt from tax under section 115BBC(2)(b) of the Income Tax Act, holding the trust is both a religious and a charitable institution.

sources.title: Vyakti Vikas Kendra India Vs. Manoj Misra (D) & Ors., Civil Appeal No. 683 of 2018 [August 22, 2026]
sources.note: Full judgment of Satish Chandra Sharma J. (for the Bench with Nongmeikapam Kotiswar Singh J.). Records that the appellant's correct legal name is "Vyakti Vikas Kendra, India" and that "Art of Living International Centre" is a centre it runs; the World Culture Festival (11-13 March 2016) was held on 25 hectares of active Yamuna floodplain after DDA permission; the NGT's interim order of 09.03.2016 imposing Rs 5 crore environmental compensation; the expert committee's shifting reports (22.02.2016, 28.07.2016, 28.11.2016) and a third, government-official committee's report of 28.07.2017 finding no significant damage; the NGT's final judgment of 07.12.2017 (OA Nos. 65/2016, 76/2016, 81/2016) holding the appellant liable for restoration/rehabilitation; and the Supreme Court's reasons for setting that judgment aside - no established causal link, pre-existing degradation, and improper conflation of "restoration" and "rehabilitation" - with a direction that DDA refund the Rs 5 crore within four weeks while continuing its own rehabilitation programme.

sources.title: Supreme Court Sets Aside NGT Order Holding 'Art Of Living' Liable For Yamuna Riverplain Damage; Directs Rs 5 Crore Refund
sources.note: Reports the 22 August 2026 judgment (2026 LiveLaw (SC) 847) and its central holding.

sources.title: Supreme Court sets aside NGT order against Art of Living over Yamuna floodplain damage, orders refund of ₹5 crore compensation
sources.note: Reports the judgment and that DDA had, per the Court's 20.04.2023 order, already carried out restoration of the allotted area at a reported cost of Rs 8.03 crore.

sources.title: 'Patience pays. Truth triumphs,' says Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar after SC sets aside NGT order against Art of Living over Yamuna floodplain damage
sources.note: Quotes Sri Sri Ravi Shankar's reaction to the judgment.

sources.title: Art of Living responsible for damaging Yamuna floodplains: NGT
sources.note: Reports the 7 December 2017 NGT judgment (bench of Justice Swatanter Kumar, Chairperson, Justice Jawad Rahim and expert member B.S. Sajwan) holding the Foundation responsible for the damage, and that the Rs 5 crore already deposited would be used by DDA for restoration.

sources.title: Damage by Art of Living will take 10 yrs to fix: NGT panel
sources.note: Reports the expert committee (headed by Shashi Shekhar, then Union Water Resources Secretary) estimate that repairing the damage to the Yamuna floodplains from the March 2016 festival would cost more than Rs 42 crore and take at least ten years.

sources.title: Art of Living will challenge tribunal's ₹5 cr penalty order
sources.note: Reports the 9 March 2016 NGT interim order permitting the World Culture Festival to proceed on payment of Rs 5 crore environmental compensation, two days before the event.

sources.title: AoL pays Rs 5 crore compensation to NGT but says they didn't damage Yamuna floodplains
sources.note: The organisation's own contemporaneous account and defence at the time of the 2016 NGT proceedings; used only for the subject's response.

sources.title: Uttar Pradesh government orders probe into Hathras stampede incident
sources.publisher: News on AIR (Prasar Bharati, Government of India)
sources.note: Government broadcaster's report of the state government's actions; gives 121 deaths and 28 seriously injured, the ADG (Agra Zone) committee and the 24-hour reporting deadline. Does not mention Surajpal by name.

sources.title: UP Police arrests Dev Prakash Madhukar in connection with tragic stampede in Hathras
sources.publisher: News on AIR (Prasar Bharati, Government of India)
sources.note: Names Madhukar as the main accused in the FIR; 121 deaths; six other organising-committee members arrested the previous day. Does not say whether Surajpal is named in the FIR.

sources.title: UP government suspends 6 officials in Hathras stampede case
sources.publisher: News on AIR (Prasar Bharati, Government of India)
sources.note: SIT report found "negligence by event organizers is the main reason"; local administration also held accountable; "a conspiracy is not denied, but in-depth investigation is needed". No mention of Surajpal.

sources.title: UP Police files chargesheet in Hathras stampede case; Surajpal not included
sources.note: Lists the 11 accused, quotes ASP Ashok Kumar Singh confirming the chargesheet and saying investigation is ongoing; gives FIR sections; carries the ANI video statement of 17 July 2024.

sources.title: 'Bhole Baba' appears before judicial commission, BJP MLA escorts him in SUV
sources.note: Appearance before the commission in Lucknow on 10 October 2024; not named in FIR; lawyer A.P. Singh's statement; BJP MLA Babu Ram Paswan (Puranpur) escorted him; UP Congress reaction.

sources.title: 'Not ruling out criminal conspiracy': Judicial panel report on Hathras stampede tabled in UP Assembly
sources.note: 1,670-page report tabled 5 March 2025; "has not mentioned any lapses on the part of the preacher"; blames organisers, local police and administration; recommends SIT probe of conspiracy angle.

sources.title: Judicial panel probing Hathras stampede blames administration for 'serious lapses', not 'Bhole Baba'
sources.note: Report "refused to name any individual or officer as responsible"; rejected toxic-spray theory; quotes the passage on the affidavit given by Bhole Baba's counsel; recommends a law against superstition.

sources.title: Judicial commission rejects claims that 'toxic spray' led to Hathras stampede
sources.note: Report tabled in the UP Legislative Assembly on 5 March 2025; commission said the call to collect "charan raj" was the main reason the crowd lost control; Surajpal named neither in the FIR nor in the chargesheet.

sources.title: Gopikas, 'healing' hand pumps & Jatav votes — journey through UP villages under Bhole Baba's 'spell'
sources.note: Retired inspector Tejveer Singh Yadav's account of the 18 March 2000 Shahganj (Agra) case; FIR under DMR Act ss.2(c), 7 and IPC 109 against six including Surajpal and his wife; chargesheet, reinvestigation, then final report by a CO-rank officer. Page fetched through a Google Translate proxy because theprint.in serves a browser check.

sources.title: Hathras stampede: Bhole Baba claimed he could revive dead, was held
sources.note: Quotes Shahganj SHO Tejveer Singh on the arrest of Surajpal, his wife and four others; IPC 109 and DMR Act. Dates the episode to 1998, whereas ThePrint (src-09) dates it to 18 March 2000.

sources.title: Hathras stampede tragedy: UP Police register FIR, names 'mukhya sevadar' Devprakash Madhukar, other organisers
sources.note: FIR filed at Sikandra Rao police station late on 2 July 2024 under BNS 105, 110, 126(2), 223 and 238, naming Madhukar and other organisers.

sources.title: UP govt forms 3-member judicial commission to probe Hathras stampede incident
sources.note: Commission formed 3 July 2024 under retired Allahabad HC judge Brijesh Kumar Srivastava with Hemant Rao and Bhavesh Kumar as members; two-month deadline.

sources.title: Hathras stampede: Bhole Baba gets 'clean chit', SIT blames organisers
sources.note: 850-page SIT report "did not find any fault" with Surajpal and "nowhere mentioned" him; blamed organisers and local administration; did not rule out conspiracy.

sources.title: Mayawati questions exclusion of Bhole Baba's name in Hathras stampede charge sheet
sources.note: Quotes Mayawati's X post of 3 October 2024 in Hindi and English.

sources.title: Hathras stampede: Lawyer says Baba in UP, not 'absconding'
sources.note: Lawyer A.P. Singh's statements in Aligarh; a senior police official said police would question Surajpal if his name came up in the investigation.

sources.title: Hathras stampede: 96-hours later, Bhole Baba says he is 'saddened' by deaths
sources.note: Surajpal's first video statement after the stampede.

sources.title: 'Truth will come out': Surajpal aka Bhole Baba on probe into Hathras stampede
sources.note: Wire agency's own report of its interview at Kasganj on 17 July 2024; the same statement is carried by Business Standard (src-04).

sources.title: Stampede triggered by toxic substance sprayed at satsang: Surajpal's lawyer
sources.note: Lawyer A.P. Singh's "poisonous substance" allegation.

sources.title: Hathras: SIT doesn't rule out 'big conspiracy' behind stampede
sources.note: SIT findings and the six officials suspended, by post.

sources.title: Supreme Court refuses to entertain PIL for probe into Hathras stampede, asks petitioner to approach HC
sources.note: Vishal Tiwari v. Union of India, W.P.(C) 428/2024; bench of CJI Chandrachud, Pardiwala and Misra JJ; liberty to approach the High Court under Article 226.

sources.title: 'Explain why aren't you liable': Allahabad HC summons DM, SP in Hathras stampede case
sources.note: Justice Shekhar Kumar Yadav's order of 6 January 2025 in the bail plea of accused Manju Devi; FIR registered on the complaint of SI Brijesh Pandey. The order concerns officials and organisers, not Surajpal.

sources.title: Hathras stampede: Court frames charges against 11 accused, trial to begin on August 18
sources.note: Charges framed by Additional Sessions Judge (Court No. I) Mahendra Srivastava; sections; 676 witnesses; all 11 on bail; Surajpal named neither in the FIR of 2 July 2024 nor in the chargesheet of 1 October 2024.

sources.title: Uttar Pradesh court fixes November 27 as next date of hearing in Hathras stampede case
sources.note: Trial under way before ASJ Mahendra Srivastava; police witnesses being examined; all 11 accused on bail.

sources.title: In Hathras stampede aftermath, how 'Bhole Baba' has divided major parties in UP
sources.note: CM Adityanath's "sajjan" remark; reports that the SIT report mentions a notice served at Surajpal's Mainpuri ashram to which he did not respond; statements of BJP MP Anoop Valmiki and SP district president Devendra Kumar Kushwaha.

sources.title: Hathras stampede: Satsang organiser was in touch with several political parties, say U.P. Police
sources.note: SP Hathras Nipun Agarwal on Madhukar's political contacts; CM Adityanath's quote; BJP affiliates circulated photos of Akhilesh Yadav at an earlier satsang.

sources.title: Akhilesh Yadav blames Yogi Adityanath government for deaths at Hathras stampede
sources.note: Akhilesh Yadav's statement of 3 July 2024 (via ANI); the FIR did not name Bhole Baba.

sources.title: Blame game over Bhole Baba: Yogi calls out godman's 'political links', Akhilesh slams 'needless arrests'
sources.note: Quotes of Adityanath (3 July 2024) and Akhilesh Yadav (6 July 2024); notes Akhilesh had posted photos from a Bhole Baba event on 3 January 2023. Page fetched through a Google Translate proxy because theprint.in serves a browser check.

sources.title: 'I'm innocent': Bhole Baba appears before judicial commission in Hathras stampede case
sources.note: Two-hour closed-door session; 1,100 affidavits submitted; arrived with BJP MLA Babu Ram Paswan; lawyer A.P. Singh's statements.

sources.title: Hathras tragedy: Cop-turned-preacher Bhole Baba attracted large number of followers in western UP
sources.note: Identity facts from CO Patiyali Vijay Kumar Rana - real name Surajpal, native of Bahadur Nagar, Kasganj, left the police in the late 1990s; SDM and DM statements on the permission.

sources.title: Hathras stampede: UP govt suspends six officials after SIT submits report
sources.note: SIT of ADG (Agra Zone) Anupam Kulshreshtha and Divisional Commissioner (Aligarh) Chaitra V; 125 statements; report "did not include" Surajpal "among those found guilty"; names of the six suspended officials.

sources.title: Hathras stampede 2024 judicial report submitted to UP government
sources.note: Report handed to the state government in February 2025; official figures of 121 dead including 112 women and at least seven children, over 80 injured.

sources.title: India: Rape accused BJP leader Chinmayanand arrested from UP ashram, sent to 14-day judicial custody
sources.note: Reports the Supreme Court's suo motu cognisance of the law student's case, its order to the Uttar Pradesh government to form a Special Investigation Team and provide security to her family, and Chinmayanand's arrest by the SIT from his Mumuksha Ashram on Friday 20 September 2019, followed by 14-day judicial custody.

sources.title: Allahabad HC grants bail to BJP leader Swami Chinmayanand in alleged rape case of law student
sources.note: Reports the Allahabad High Court granting Chinmayanand bail on Monday 3 February 2020, about five months after his arrest, with a direction for day-to-day trial at the Shahjahanpur district court; records that the law student had earlier been granted bail and that Chinmayanand alleged she and two friends had tried to blackmail him.

sources.title: Witnesses turn hostile, rape accused BJP MP Chinmayanand acquitted
sources.note: Reports the 26 March 2021 acquittal by Special Judge P.K. Rai on the ground the prosecution could not prove the case beyond reasonable doubt and the complainant had turned hostile; records the FIR of 27 August 2019, arrest on 20 September 2019, the February 2020 Allahabad High Court bail order and its reasoning (Justice Rahul Chaturvedi), and the 25 August 2019 counter-FIR for extortion lodged by advocate Om Singh, on which the accused were acquitted the same day for lack of evidence.

sources.title: Special Court Acquits Ex-BJP Leader Chinmayanand in Rape Case
sources.note: Confirms the 26 March 2021 acquittal in the rape and extortion case filed by the law student, the SIT formed on Supreme Court directions, and the chargesheet filed against Chinmayanand.

sources.title: Allahabad High Court Upholds Rejection Of State's Plea To Withdraw Rape Case Against Swami Chinmayanand, Slams UP Govt
sources.note: Justice Rahul Chaturvedi. Records that the FIR was lodged by a disciple alleging rape, administering intoxicants and forced abortions; a chargesheet under IPC 376 and 506 was filed and the CJM Shahjahanpur took cognizance in December 2011; the High Court stayed proceedings in December 2012 on Chinmayanand's own 482 CrPC petition; that stay was vacated in February 2018 when Chinmayanand withdrew his petition; the Uttar Pradesh government then directed the Public Prosecutor to seek withdrawal of the prosecution, an application the Chief Judicial Magistrate rejected; and the High Court upheld that rejection on 30 September 2022, criticising the Senior Public Prosecutor for having "danced to the tune" of the state government.

sources.title: Former Union Minister Chinmayanand acquitted in 2011 rape case, Lawyer

cases.titleEn: State v. Billu Ram alias Amarpuri (Tohana FIR of 19 July 2018; Fast Track Court, Fatehabad)
cases.titleHi: राज्य बनाम बिल्लू राम उर्फ अमरपुरी (टोहाना एफआईआर, 19 जुलाई 2018; फास्ट ट्रैक कोर्ट, फतेहाबाद)
cases.court: Fast Track Court (Additional District Judge Balwant Singh), Fatehabad
cases.status: Reported by The Tribune as convicted on 5 January 2023 and sentenced on 10 January 2023; defence counsel said the verdict would be challenged in the Punjab and Haryana High Court; the convict died in custody on 8 May 2024. Held at allegation tier because no court or official record has yet been obtained.
cases.sentenceOrRemedy: 14 years' rigorous imprisonment under POCSO s.6, 7 years each on two rape counts (reported as IPC 376/376-C) and 5 years under IT Act s.67A, all concurrent, with a fine of Rs 35,000; acquitted of the Arms Act charge (as reported).
cases.appealStatus: Defence counsel Gajender Pandey told The Tribune on 11 January 2023 that the verdict would be challenged in the High Court. No Punjab and Haryana High Court order or case-status record could be located as of 2026-09-09; the convict died on 8 May 2024.
cases.summaryEn: Tohana city police registered a case on 19 July 2018, on the complaint of the then SHO, under IPC sections 292, 293, 294, 376, 384 and 509 and section 67A of the IT Act, after a video clip allegedly showing Amarpuri with a woman reached the police; POCSO Act sections were added when a minor was identified among the victims. Police told reporters that around 120 video clips were recovered and that six women were traced from the footage, of whom five agreed to depose. The Tribune reported that the Fast Track Court at Fatehabad convicted him on 5 January 2023 on the evidence of three women including a minor, and on 10 January 2023 sentenced him to 14 years' imprisonment with a fine of Rs 35,000, the sentences running concurrently, with about four and a half years already served to be deducted. His counsel argued the case rested on CDs without a section 65B certificate and said the verdict would be appealed. No court judgment or official statement has yet been fetched for this file.
cases.summaryHi: टोहाना शहर पुलिस ने 19 जुलाई 2018 को तत्कालीन थाना प्रभारी की शिकायत पर आईपीसी की धारा 292, 293, 294, 376, 384, 509 और आईटी अधिनियम की धारा 67A के तहत मामला दर्ज किया, जब कथित रूप से अमरपुरी को एक महिला के साथ दिखाने वाली एक वीडियो क्लिप पुलिस तक पहुँची; पीड़ितों में एक नाबालिग की पहचान होने पर पॉक्सो अधिनियम की धाराएँ जोड़ी गईं। पुलिस ने पत्रकारों को बताया कि लगभग 120 वीडियो क्लिप बरामद हुईं और फुटेज से छह महिलाओं का पता लगाया गया, जिनमें से पाँच गवाही देने को तैयार हुईं। द ट्रिब्यून के अनुसार फतेहाबाद की फास्ट ट्रैक अदालत ने 5 जनवरी 2023 को एक नाबालिग सहित तीन महिलाओं की गवाही के आधार पर उन्हें दोषी ठहराया और 10 जनवरी 2023 को 14 वर्ष के कारावास तथा 35,000 रुपये जुर्माने की सज़ा सुनाई; सभी सज़ाएँ साथ-साथ चलेंगी और लगभग साढ़े चार वर्ष की पहले से काटी गई अवधि घटाई जाएगी। उनके वकील ने कहा कि मामला बिना धारा 65B प्रमाणपत्र वाली सीडी पर टिका है और फैसले के विरुद्ध अपील की जाएगी। इस फ़ाइल के लिए अभी तक कोई अदालती निर्णय या आधिकारिक बयान प्राप्त नहीं हुआ है।
